title.zh: 卷四百七十八 列傳第二百三十七 世家一 南唐李氏李景(子:煜 從善 從誧 從弟:季操 孫:仲寓 附:舒元 韓熙載 馮謐 潘佑 皇甫繼勳 周惟簡)
title.en: Volume 478 Biographies 237: Hereditary Houses 1 - Southern Tang and Li clans Li Jing (son: Yu, relative Shan, relative Bu, nephew: Ji Cao, grandson: Zhong Yu, relatives: Shu Yuan, Han Xizai, Feng Mi, Pan You, Huang Fujixun, Zhou Weijian)
title.raw: 卷四百七十八 列傳第二百三十七 世家一 南唐李氏李景(子:煜 從善 從誧 從弟:季操 孫:仲寓 附:舒元 韓熙載 馮謐 潘佑 皇甫繼勳 周惟簡) Volume 478 Biographies 237: Hereditary Houses 1 - Southern Tang and Li clans Li Jing (son: Yu, relative Shan, relative Bu, nephew: Ji Cao, grandson: Zhong Yu, relatives: Shu Yuan, Han Xizai, Feng Mi, Pan You, Huang Fujixun, Zhou Weijian)

sentences.zh: 世家一○南唐李氏

translations.literal: Hereditary Houses 1 ○ Southern Tang and the Li Clan
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary Houses 1: The Southern Tang and the House of Li

sentences.zh: 唐自安、史之亂，藩鎮專製，百有餘年，浸成割據。

translations.literal: From the rebellions of An Lushan and Shi Siming in the Tang, the military governors held exclusive power for more than a hundred years, gradually becoming regional partitions.
translations.idiomatic: After the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellions shattered the Tang, military governors ruled autonomously for over a century, and the realm slowly fragmented into rival domains.

sentences.zh: 及巢賊蹂躪，郡邑丘墟。

translations.literal: When the Huang Chao bandits ravaged the land, commanderies and districts became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao's rebels swept the empire, cities and towns lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 降臻五季，豪傑蜂午，各挾智力，擅為封疆，自製位號，以爭長雄。

translations.literal: Descending to the Five Dynasties, heroes swarmed like bees at noon, each wielding wisdom and strength, usurping territories for themselves, establishing their own titles and ranks, to contend for supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: By the Five Dynasties, rival warlords abounded; each relied on wit and force, carved out his own territory, proclaimed his own titles, and strove for mastery.

sentences.zh: 天厭禍亂，授宋大柄。

translations.literal: Heaven grew weary of calamity and turmoil and bestowed the great mandate upon Song.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had had enough of chaos and entrusted the great mandate to the Song.

sentences.zh: 太祖命將出師，十餘年間，南平荊、楚，西取巴、蜀，劉鋹既俘，李氏納款。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor ordered generals to campaign; within more than ten years, he pacified the south with Jing and Chu, seized Ba and Shu in the west; once Liu Chang was captured, the Li clan submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent his armies forth; within little more than a decade the south was pacified—Jing and Chu fell, Ba and Shu were taken in the west—and once Liu Chang was captured, the House of Li tendered its submission.

sentences.zh: 至於太宗，吳越請吏，漳、泉來歸，薄伐太原，遂僨北漢，而海內一矣！

translations.literal: As for Taizong, Wuyue requested officials, Zhangzhou and Quanzhou returned, he made a brief expedition against Taiyuan and thereby extinguished Northern Han, and within the seas there was unity!
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, Wuyue asked to be administered directly, Zhang and Quan came back into the fold, Taiyuan was attacked and Northern Han destroyed, and the empire was united at last.

sentences.zh: 王稱《東都事略》用東漢隗囂、公孫述例，置孟昶、劉鋹等於列傳，舊史因之。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng's Eastern Capital Affairs followed the Eastern Han examples of Wei Xiao and Gongsun Shu, placing Meng Chang, Liu Chang, and the like in biographies; the old histories followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng's Eastern Capital Affairs followed the Eastern Han precedent of treating Wei Xiao and Gongsun Shu in biographical chapters rather than as central dynasties, placing Meng Chang, Liu Chang, and others in ordinary biographies—and later official histories did the same.

sentences.zh: 今仿歐陽修《五代史記》，列之世家。

translations.literal: Now, imitating Ouyang Xiu's Historical Records of the Five Dynasties, they are arranged in hereditary houses.
translations.idiomatic: Following Ouyang Xiu's Historical Records of the Five Dynasties, this history places them in the Hereditary Houses section.

sentences.zh: 凡諸國治亂之原，天下離合之勢，有足鑒者，悉著於篇。

translations.literal: All origins of order and disorder in the various states and trends of union and separation in the realm that are worth taking as mirrors are fully set forth in these chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever in these states' rise and fall, or in the realm's shifting unity and division, is worth heeding as a lesson is set out in these pages.

sentences.zh: 其子孫諸臣事業有可考者，各疏本國之下。

translations.literal: Where the careers of sons, grandsons, and various officials can be examined, each is set out below its native state.
translations.idiomatic: Sons, grandsons, and officials whose careers can be traced are each treated under their respective state.

sentences.zh: 作《列國世家》。

translations.literal: The composition is "Hereditary Houses of the Various States."
translations.idiomatic: Thus was compiled the Hereditary Houses of the Various States.

sentences.zh: 南唐李景，本名景通，後改為璟。

translations.literal: Li Jing of Southern Tang had the original name Jingtong and later changed it to Jing (written with the jade radical).
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing of Southern Tang was born Jingtong and later changed his name to Jing (the character with the jade radical).

sentences.zh: 避周廟諱，復改為景。

translations.literal: To avoid the temple taboo of Zhou, he again changed it to Jing (written with the sun radical).
translations.idiomatic: To avoid a Zhou dynasty temple taboo he changed it again to Jing (the character with the sun radical).

sentences.zh: 父，吳楊行密將徐溫養子，冒姓徐氏，名知誥，《五代史》有傳。

translations.literal: His father was the adopted son of Xu Wen, a general of Wu under Yang Xingmi, who took the surname Xu falsely and was named Zhigao; he has a biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Xu Zhigao, Xu Wen's adopted heir and a Wu general under Yang Xingmi who had assumed the surname Xu; he has a biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 景十餘歲，以父任駕部郎中、諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Jing was a little more than ten years old, through his father's position he became Director of the Chariot Office and a general of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his teens, Jing received appointments as Director of the Chariot Office and as a guards general through his father's influence.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成二年，溫卒，遂專吳政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng under Later Tang, Wen died, and he thereupon monopolized Wu government.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng of Later Tang, Xu Wen died, and Zhigao seized sole control of Wu.

sentences.zh: 將出鎮，欲以國事付景，拜兵部尚書、參知政事。

translations.literal: When he was about to go out to a garrison post, wishing to entrust state affairs to Jing, he appointed him Minister of War and Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving to take up a provincial command, he meant to entrust state affairs to Jing and appointed him Minister of War and Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 出鎮金陵，遷景司徒、平章事、知內外左右諸軍事。

translations.literal: Going out to garrison Jinling, he promoted Jing to Grand Preceptor, Grand Councilor, and Director of All Military Affairs Within and Without.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to garrison Jinling, he promoted Jing to Grand Preceptor, Grand Councilor, and director of all military affairs at court and in the field.

sentences.zh: 頃之，亦赴金陵，為中外諸軍副都統，受吳禪，國號大齊，改元升元，僭帝號，居金陵。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, he also went to Jinling, became Deputy Overall Commander of All Armies at Court and in the Provinces, received the Wu abdication, took the state name Great Qi, changed the era name to Shengyuan, usurped the imperial title, and dwelt at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he too moved to Jinling, became deputy overall commander of all armies, accepted the Wu abdication, declared the state Great Qi with the era name Shengyuan, took an imperial title, and made Jinling his capital.

sentences.zh: 自雲唐宗室建王恪之後，下令復姓李氏，國號唐。

translations.literal: He claimed descent from Prince Li Ke of Jian of the Tang imperial house, issued an order to restore the surname Li, and changed the state name to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Claiming descent from Tang's Prince of Jian, Li Ke, he ordered the restoration of the surname Li and renamed the state Tang.

sentences.zh: 封景吳王、諸道元帥、錄尚書事，改封齊王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Jing as Prince of Wu, Commander-in-Chief of All Circuits, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, then changed the enfeoffment to Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Jing as Prince of Wu and commander-in-chief of all circuits and recorder of the masters of writing, later changing the title to Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 昪立七年卒，景襲位，改元保大，尊母宋氏為皇太后，立妻鍾氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Seven years after Bian's establishment he died; Jing succeeded to the position, changed the era name to Baoda, honored his mother Lady Song as empress dowager, and installed his wife Lady Zhong as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Bian died seven years after taking power; Jing succeeded him, adopted the era name Baoda, honored his mother Lady Song as empress dowager, and made his wife Lady Zhong empress.

sentences.zh: 用宋齊丘、周宗為宰相，郊祀天地。

translations.literal: He employed Song Qiqiu and Zhou Zong as prime ministers and performed suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Song Qiqiu and Zhou Zong prime ministers and performed the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 天福末，遣其將祖思全、何洙侵福建漳、泉之地。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianfu, he sent his generals Zu Siquan and He Zhu to invade the Zhang and Quan districts of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianfu era he sent generals Zu Siquan and He Zhu to attack Zhang and Quan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，李守貞以河中叛，潛遣舒元、楊訥間道求援於景。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou under Han, Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong and secretly sent Shu Yuan and Yang Ne by hidden routes to seek aid from Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyou era of Later Han, Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and secretly sent Shu Yuan and Yang Ne by back roads to ask Jing for help.

sentences.zh: 景命其將李金全、郭全義出師應之。

translations.literal: Jing ordered his generals Li Jinquan and Guo Quanyi to lead armies out in response.
translations.idiomatic: Jing ordered his generals Li Jinquan and Guo Quanyi to march out in support.

sentences.zh: 金全以聲勢不接，初不願行，景固遣之。

translations.literal: Jinquan, because momentum did not connect, at first was unwilling to go; Jing firmly sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan at first refused to go, judging that his forces could not link up with Shouzhen's, but Jing insisted and sent him anyway.

sentences.zh: 至沭陽，聞守貞敗，乃還。

translations.literal: Reaching Shuyang, he heard that Shouzhen had been defeated and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Shuyang he learned that Shouzhen had already been defeated and turned back.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，景又遣其將邊鎬平湖湘，尋復失之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun under Zhou, Jing again sent his general Bian Hao to pacify Lake and Xiang, but soon lost it again.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun era of Later Zhou, Jing again sent Bian Hao to pacify Hunan, but soon lost the region once more.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年，周世宗征淮南，破景眾於正陽，遂進圍壽州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiande, the Shizong Emperor of Zhou campaigned against Huainan, defeated Jing's masses at Zhengyang, and then advanced to besiege Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiande, Zhou Shizong marched against Huainan, routed Jing's army at Zhengyang, and pressed on to besiege Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖時總禁兵，破景將何延錫於渦口，又擒皇甫暉於滁州。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu commanded the palace guards, defeated Jing's general He Yansi at Wokou, and also captured Huangfu Hui at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, then commanding the palace guards, defeated Jing's general He Yansi at Wokou and captured Huangfu Hui at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 景大懼，遣其臣鍾謨、李德明奉表原為附庸。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly afraid and sent his ministers Zhong Mo and Li Deming with a memorial asking to become a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Jing sent his ministers Zhong Mo and Li Deming with a memorial offering to become a vassal state.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又遣其臣孫晟、王崇質奉表獻濠、壽、泗、楚、光、海六州之地，願罷兵，世宗未之許。

translations.literal: Before long, he again sent his ministers Sun Sheng and Wang Chongzhi with a memorial offering the six prefectures of Hao, Shou, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai, wishing to halt the armies; Shizong did not grant this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he sent Sun Sheng and Wang Chongzhi with a memorial ceding the six prefectures of Hao, Shou, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai and asking for an armistice, but Shizong refused.

sentences.zh: 四年春，世宗大破景軍於紫金山，降其將朱元，克壽州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, Shizong greatly defeated Jing's army at Purple Gold Mountain, accepted the surrender of his general Zhu Yuan, and captured Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year Shizong routed Jing's army at Purple Gold Mountain, won over his general Zhu Yuan, and took Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，又克濠、泗二州。

translations.literal: In winter, he again captured the two prefectures of Hao and Si.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he also captured Hao and Si.

sentences.zh: 五年春，改元中興。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, he changed the era name to Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year Jing changed the era name to Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又改元交泰。

translations.literal: Before long, he again changed the era name to Jiaotai.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he changed it again to Jiaotai.

sentences.zh: 是春，周師克楚州，又進克揚州。

translations.literal: That spring, the Zhou army captured Chuzhou and then advanced to capture Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That spring the Zhou forces took Chuzhou and then advanced to capture Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 將議濟江，景大懼，請盡割江北之地，畫江為界，稱臣於中朝，歲貢土物數十萬，世宗許之。

translations.literal: When they were about to discuss crossing the river, Jing was greatly afraid and requested to cede all territory north of the river, draw the river as a boundary, declare himself a subject of the central court, and present tens of thousands in annual tribute of local products; Shizong granted this.
translations.idiomatic: As the Zhou prepared to cross the Yangzi, Jing in terror offered to surrender all territory north of the river, accept the river as the border, submit as a vassal of the central court, and pay annual tribute in the tens of thousands; Shizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 始稟周之正朔，上表稱唐國主。

translations.literal: He thereupon received Zhou's calendar and reign title and submitted a memorial styling himself Lord of the Tang State.
translations.idiomatic: He then adopted Zhou's calendar and reign title and addressed himself in memorials as Lord of the Tang State.

sentences.zh: 世宗答書用唐報回鶻可汗之制，雲「皇帝恭問江南國主」，臨汴水置懷信驛以待其使。

translations.literal: Shizong's reply used the Tang form for addressing the Uyghur qaghan, saying "The Emperor respectfully inquires of the Lord of the Jiangnan State," and set up the Huaixin courier station by the Bian River to await his envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's reply followed the Tang formula used for the Uyghur qaghan—"The Emperor respectfully inquires of the Lord of the Jiangnan State"—and established the Huaixin courier station on the Bian River to receive his envoys.

sentences.zh: 景又上言世宗，請傳位於世子冀，世宗賜書勉諭之乃止。

translations.literal: Jing again addressed Shizong, asking to pass the throne to his heir Li Ji; Shizong bestowed a letter encouraging and instructing him, and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: Jing also asked Shizong's permission to abdicate in favor of his heir Li Ji; Shizong wrote back urging him to remain on the throne, and Jing desisted.

sentences.zh: 景既失淮南之地，頗躁憤，惡其大臣宋齊丘、陳覺、李征古，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Once Jing had lost the Huainan territory, he was quite restless and resentful, hated his great ministers Song Qiqiu, Chen Jue, and Li Zhenggu, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: After losing Huainan, Jing grew restless and bitter; he turned on his chief ministers Song Qiqiu, Chen Jue, and Li Zhenggu and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 六年十月，冀卒，命禦廚使張延範充使吊祭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year, Ji died; he ordered the imperial kitchen commissioner Zhang Yanfan to serve as envoy for condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixth year Li Ji died; Zhou ordered the imperial kitchen commissioner Zhang Yanfan to go as condolence envoy.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，太祖受命，即遣使以書諭景。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong, Taizu received the Mandate and immediately sent envoys with a letter to instruct Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianlong, as soon as Taizu received the Mandate, he sent envoys with a letter to notify Jing.

sentences.zh: 初，顯德中，江南將校相繼來降，周成等三十四人皆在京師，至是遣歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Xiande, Jiangnan officers and commanders came over in succession; Zhou Cheng and thirty-four others were all in the capital, and at this time they were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiande many Jiangnan officers had defected to Zhou; thirty-four men including Zhou Cheng had remained in the capital, and now Taizu sent them home.

sentences.zh: 三月，景遣使貢絹二萬匹、銀萬兩，賀登極。

translations.literal: In the third month, Jing sent envoys presenting twenty thousand bolts of silk and ten thousand taels of silver to congratulate his accession to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Jing sent tribute of twenty thousand bolts of silk and ten thousand taels of silver to congratulate Taizu on taking the throne.

sentences.zh: 及澤、潞平，景又貢銀五千兩為賀，七月還京，又貢金器五百兩、銀器三千兩、羅紈千匹、絹五千匹，又遣其禮部郎中龔慎儀貢乘輿服御物。

translations.literal: When Ze and Lu were pacified, Jing again presented five thousand taels of silver in congratulations; in the seventh month, on returning to the capital, he again presented five hundred taels of gold vessels, three thousand taels of silver vessels, a thousand bolts of gauze silk, and five thousand bolts of silk, and also sent his Ministry of Rites director Gong Shenyi to present imperial carriage garments and utensils.
translations.idiomatic: When Ze and Lu were pacified Jing sent another five thousand taels of silver in congratulation; when Taizu returned to the capital in the seventh month, Jing sent five hundred taels of gold vessels, three thousand taels of silver vessels, a thousand bolts of gauze, five thousand bolts of silk, and his Ministry of Rites director Gong Shenyi with imperial carriage regalia as tribute.

sentences.zh: 每歲冬、正、端午、長春節皆以土產珍異、金銀器用、繒帛、片茶為貢。

translations.literal: Every year at the winter solstice, New Year, Dragon Boat Festival, and Long Spring Festival he presented local rare products, gold and silver utensils, silks, and pressed tea as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Each year at the winter solstice, New Year, Dragon Boat Festival, and Long Spring Festival he sent tribute of local exotica, gold and silver wares, silks, and pressed tea.

sentences.zh: 每景及錢俶遣親屬入貢，皆御前殿曲宴以寵之。

translations.literal: Whenever Jing and Qian Chu sent relatives to present tribute, they were all given intimate banquets in the imperial presence hall as a mark of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jing or Qian Chu sent kinsmen with tribute, Taizu entertained them at intimate banquets in the imperial hall to show his favor.

sentences.zh: 景生日，遣使賜以金幣及賜羊萬口、馬三百疋、橐駝三十，以為常制。

translations.literal: On Jing's birthday, envoys were sent to bestow gold coins and also ten thousand sheep, three hundred horses, and thirty camels, as a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On Jing's birthday the court routinely sent envoys with gold coins, ten thousand sheep, three hundred horses, and thirty camels.

sentences.zh: 是年，親征李重進，駐蹕廣陵，遣其左僕射嚴續來犒師。

translations.literal: That year, he personally campaigned against Li Chongjin, halted the imperial progress at Guangling, and Jing sent his Left Vice Director Yan Xu to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: That year Taizu campaigned in person against Li Chongjin and halted at Guangling; Jing sent his Left Vice Director Yan Xu to bring supplies for the army.

sentences.zh: 俄遣其子蔣國公從鎰朝行在所，又遣其戶部尚書馮延魯貢金買宴，並伶官五十人作樂上壽，又貢金銀器、金玉鞍勒、銀裝兵器及錢銀、綾絹，皆有加常數，太祖亦厚賜之。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he sent his son, the Duke of Jiangguo Congyi, to attend the mobile court; he also sent his Minister of Revenue Feng Yanlu to present gold to purchase a banquet, along with fifty musicians to perform music and offer longevity wishes, and again presented gold and silver vessels, gold and jade saddles and bridles, silver-mounted weapons, and money, silver, and damask silks—all exceeding the usual amounts—and Taizu also richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jing sent his son, Duke of Jiangguo Congyi, to the imperial camp, and his Minister of Revenue Feng Yanlu with gold to fund a banquet, fifty musicians to perform and offer birthday wishes, and extra gifts of gold and silver vessels, jade-mounted saddlery, silver-mounted arms, cash, silver, and silks beyond the usual tribute; Taizu responded with lavish gifts in return.

sentences.zh: 初，景之襲父位也，屬中原多故，盧文進、李金全、皇甫暉之徒皆奔於景。

translations.literal: When Jing first succeeded to his father's position, the central plains were beset by many troubles; Lu Wenjin, Li Jinquan, Huangfu Hui, and the like all fled to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing first succeeded his father, the central plains were in turmoil, and men such as Lu Wenjin, Li Jinquan, and Huangfu Hui all fled to his court.

sentences.zh: 跨據江、淮三十餘州，擅魚鹽之利，即山鑄錢，物力富盛。

translations.literal: He straddled more than thirty prefectures along the Yangzi and Huai, monopolized the profits of fish and salt, cast coin at the mountains, and his material strength was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He held more than thirty prefectures along the Yangzi and Huai, controlled the salt and fishing trades, minted coin from mountain copper, and enjoyed great material wealth.

sentences.zh: 嘗試貢士《高祖入關詩》，頗有窺覦中土之意。

translations.literal: He once tested presented scholars with the poem "Gaozu Enters the Pass," showing considerable intent to covet the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: He once set "Gaozu Enters the Pass" as a civil examination topic, betraying his ambition to seize the central plains.

sentences.zh: 自世宗平淮甸，浸以衰弱。

translations.literal: From the time Shizong pacified the Huai region, he gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong pacified Huainan, his power steadily declined.

sentences.zh: 及太祖平揚州，日習馬舫戰艦於京城之南池，景懼甚。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Yangzhou, he daily drilled horse-boats and warships in the southern pond of the capital; Jing was very afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took Yangzhou, the Song court daily drilled war junks in the southern pond of the capital, and Jing was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 其小臣杜著頗有辭辨，偽作商人，由建安渡來歸；

translations.literal: His petty official Du Zhuo was quite eloquent in debate, falsely posed as a merchant, and came over by crossing from Jian'an;
translations.idiomatic: A minor official of his, Du Zhuo, was clever with words; disguised as a merchant he crossed from Jian'an and defected to Song;

sentences.zh: 又彭澤令薛良坐事責授池州文學，亦挺身來奔，獻《平南策》，景聞之益懼。

translations.literal: Also the magistrate of Pengze, Xue Liang, because of an offense was demoted to literary officer of Chizhou, also came in person to flee, presented a "Strategy for Pacifying the South," and when Jing heard of it he grew even more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: and Xue Liang, magistrate of Pengze who had been demoted to literary officer at Chizhou for an offense, also fled to Song and offered a plan to conquer the south—news that frightened Jing all the more.

sentences.zh: 太祖命斬著於下蜀市，良配隸廬州衙校，景乃安。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered Zhuo beheaded in the Lower Shu market; Liang was assigned as bondsman to a Luchou yamen guard, and only then was Jing at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had Zhuo executed in the Lower Shu market and assigned Liang to service under a Luchou yamen guard; only then did Jing feel reassured.

sentences.zh: 終以國境蹙弱，不遑寧居，遂遷於豫章。

translations.literal: In the end, because the state's borders were cramped and weak, he had no leisure to dwell in peace and therefore moved to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Ultimately, with his territory shrinking and his position insecure, he could no longer remain at ease in his capital and moved his court to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 上遣通事舍人王守正持詔撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the communications chamberlain Wang Shouzheng bearing an edict to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent communications chamberlain Wang Shouzheng with an edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 俄而景卒，其臣桂陽郡公徐邈奉遺表來上，太祖廢朝五日，遣鞍轡庫使梁義吊祭，贈賻絹三千匹。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Jing died; his minister, the Duke of Guiyang Xu Miao, presented the final memorial; Taizu suspended court for five days, sent the saddle and bridle store commissioner Liang Yi for condolences, and granted funeral gifts of three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jing died; his minister, Duke of Guiyang Xu Miao, brought his final memorial; Taizu suspended court for five days, sent saddle-store commissioner Liang Yi to offer condolences, and granted three thousand bolts of silk as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 子煜又遣其臣馮謐奉表，願追尊帝號，許之。

translations.literal: His son Yu again sent his minister Feng Mi with a memorial, wishing to posthumously honor him with an imperial title; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu then sent Feng Mi with a memorial asking to posthumously honor his father with an imperial title, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 煜乃諡景為明道崇德文宣孝皇帝，廟號元宗，陵號順陵。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon gave Jing the posthumous title Emperor Xiaowen of Illustrious Virtue in the Mingdao and Chongde traditions, with temple name Yuanzong and tomb name Shunling.
translations.idiomatic: Yu posthumously styled him Emperor Xiaowen of Illustrious Virtue in the Mingdao and Chongde traditions, with temple name Yuanzong and tomb name Shunling.

sentences.zh: 景始嗣位，以弟齊王景遂為元帥，居東宮，燕王景達為副元帥，就柩前盟約，兄弟相繼，中外庶政，並委景遂參決。

translations.literal: When Jing first succeeded to the throne, he made his younger brother, Prince of Qi Jing Sui, commander-in-chief dwelling in the Eastern Palace, and Prince of Yan Jing Da deputy commander-in-chief; before the coffin they made a covenant that brothers would succeed one another, and all civil and military affairs at court and in the provinces were entrusted to Jing Sui for joint decision.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing first took the throne he made his younger brother, Prince of Qi Jing Sui, commander-in-chief and titular heir in the Eastern Palace, with Prince of Yan Jing Da as deputy; at their father's coffin they swore that brothers would succeed in turn, and Jing Sui was given joint authority over all civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 景長子冀為東都留守，後又立景遂為太弟，景達為齊王、元帥，冀為燕王、副元帥。

translations.literal: Jing's eldest son Ji was left to guard the eastern capital; later he again installed Jing Sui as Imperial Younger Brother, Jing Da as Prince of Qi and commander-in-chief, and Ji as Prince of Yan and deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's eldest son Ji was made guardian of the eastern capital; later Jing Sui was named Imperial Younger Brother, Jing Da Prince of Qi and commander-in-chief, and Ji Prince of Yan and deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 冀鎮京口，周師征淮，吳越圍常州，冀部將敗之。

translations.literal: Ji garrisoned Jingkou; when the Zhou army campaigned against Huai, Wuyue besieged Changzhou, and Ji's subordinate generals defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was stationed at Jingkou; when Zhou marched against Huainan and Wuyue besieged Changzhou, his subordinates routed the besiegers.

sentences.zh: 景達屯濠州，丘衄遁還。

translations.literal: Jing Da encamped at Haozhou; Qiu Yin fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Da held Haozhou while Qiu Yin retreated in defeat.

sentences.zh: 及割地後，出景遂為洪州元帥，封晉王。

translations.literal: After the territorial cession, he sent Jing Sui out as commander-in-chief of Hongzhou and enfeoffed him as Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: After the cession of territory he posted Jing Sui to Hongzhou as regional commander and enfeoffed him as Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 景達撫州元帥，立冀為太子。

translations.literal: Jing Da was commander-in-chief of Fuzhou, and Ji was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Da was made commander at Fuzhou, and Ji was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 景遂尋卒，數月冀亦卒，乃立從嘉為吳王。

translations.literal: Jing Sui soon died; several months later Ji also died, and thereupon Congjia was installed as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Sui died soon afterward; a few months later Ji died as well, and Congjia was made Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，景遷洪州，立為太子監國，是秋襲位，居建康，改名煜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, Jing moved to Hongzhou; Congjia was installed as crown prince to supervise the state; that autumn he succeeded to the position, dwelt at Jiankang, and changed his name to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong, Jing moved to Hongzhou and made Congjia crown prince regent; that autumn Congjia succeeded, took up residence at Jiankang, and changed his name to Yu.

sentences.zh: 立母鍾氏為聖尊后，以鍾氏父名泰章故也，妻周氏為國后。

translations.literal: He installed his mother Lady Zhong as Sacred Honored Empress—because Lady Zhong's father's name was Taizhang—and his wife Lady Zhou as state empress.
translations.idiomatic: He made his mother Lady Zhong Sacred Honored Empress—the title avoiding the character in her father's name, Taizhang—and his wife Lady Zhou state empress.

sentences.zh: 遣戶部尚書馮謐來貢金器二千兩、銀器二腕兩、紗羅繒彩三萬匹。

translations.literal: He sent his Minister of Revenue Feng Mi to present two thousand taels of gold vessels, two thousand taels of silver vessels, and thirty thousand bolts of gauze, silk, and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his Minister of Revenue Feng Mi with two thousand taels of gold vessels, two thousand taels of silver vessels, and thirty thousand bolts of gauze, silk, and brocade as tribute.

sentences.zh: 且奉表陳紹襲之意曰：

translations.literal: Moreover he submitted a memorial stating his intent in succeeding, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial on his succession, which read:

sentences.zh: 臣本於諸子，實愧非才，自出膠庠，心疏利祿。

translations.literal: Your subject was originally among the sons and truly ashamed of lacking talent; from leaving the school of the heir apparent, his heart has been distant from profit and emolument.
translations.idiomatic: I was born one of many sons and have always known myself unworthy; since leaving the heir's school I have cared little for rank or reward.

sentences.zh: 被父兄之蔭育，樂日月以優遊，思追巢、許之餘塵，遠慕夷、齊之高義。

translations.literal: Nurtured under the shade of father and elder brothers, he delighted in passing days at ease, thinking to follow the remaining traces of Chao Fu and Xu You, and from afar admiring the lofty righteousness of Boyi and Shuqi.
translations.idiomatic: Sheltered by my father and brothers, I passed my days in leisure, hoping to follow the recluses Chao Fu and Xu You and emulating from afar the integrity of Boyi and Shuqi.

sentences.zh: 繼傾懇悃，上告先君，固匪虛詞，人多知者。

translations.literal: Again and again he poured out sincere intent and reported upward to his late father; it was certainly not empty words—many people know this.
translations.idiomatic: I told my late father again and again, in all sincerity, that I wished no part of rule; that was no empty phrase, and many can attest to it.

sentences.zh: 徒以伯仲繼沒，次第推遷，先世謂臣克習義方，既長且嫡，俾司國事，遽易年華。

translations.literal: Only because elder and younger brothers died in succession was he pushed forward in order; the previous generation said your subject had mastered moral teaching, was both eldest and legitimate, and made him administer state affairs—years suddenly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Only because my elder brothers died in turn was I pushed forward; my forebears judged that I had learned proper conduct and, as the eldest legitimate son, put me in charge of state affairs—and the years slipped away.

sentences.zh: 及乎暫赴豫章，留居建業，正儲副之位，分監撫之權，懼弗克堪，常深自勵。

translations.literal: When for a time he went to Yuzhang and remained at Jiankang, he rectified the position of heir apparent and shared supervisory and comforting authority, fearing he could not bear it and constantly urging himself deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When my father went temporarily to Yuzhang and left me at Jiankang as regent, I was confirmed as heir and given a share in government, fearing I was unequal to the task and striving constantly to do better.

sentences.zh: 不謂掩丁艱罰，遂玷纘承，因顧肯堂，不敢滅性。

translations.literal: He did not expect the sudden onset of mourning hardship and punishment, and thus stained the succession; because he looked back at the hall his father had favored, he did not dare extinguish his nature through excessive grief.
translations.idiomatic: I never imagined that bereavement would place the succession in my hands; remembering my father's hall, I did not dare let grief destroy me.

sentences.zh: 然念先世君臨江表垂二十年，中間務在倦勤，將思釋負。

translations.literal: Yet reflecting that the previous generation ruled the lands south of the Yangzi for nearly twenty years, in the midst of which he was weary of diligence and wished to lay down his burden.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I recall that my father ruled the south for nearly twenty years, growing weary in office and wishing to lay down his burden.

sentences.zh: 臣亡兄文獻太子從冀將從內禪，已決宿心，而世宗敦勸既深，議言因息。

translations.literal: Your subject's deceased elder brother, the Literary and Illustrious Crown Prince Congji, was about to follow inner abdication; his long-settled heart had been decided, but Shizong's earnest encouragement was deep, and the discussion therefore ceased.
translations.idiomatic: My late brother, Crown Prince Congji, was ready to accept abdication in my father's favor; Shizong's earnest persuasion put an end to that plan.

sentences.zh: 及陛下顯膺帝籙，彌篤睿情，方誓子孫，仰酬臨照。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty clearly received the imperial tally, his sagely affection grew even firmer; he was just then vowing that sons and grandsons would look up to repay your overseeing radiance.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty received the Mandate, my father's loyalty deepened; he vowed that his sons and grandsons would repay your gracious oversight.

sentences.zh: 則臣向於脫屣，亦匪邀名，既嗣宗枋，敢忘負荷。

translations.literal: As for your subject's former wish to cast off shoes like refuse, it was also not to invite a name; now that he has succeeded to the ancestral altar, how dare he forget the burden?
translations.idiomatic: My old wish to cast off power as one casts off worn shoes was never for reputation's sake; now that I have succeeded to the ancestral altar, how can I forget the burden I bear?

sentences.zh: 唯堅臣節，上奉天朝。

translations.literal: He will only hold fast to the subject's integrity and upward serve the celestial dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: I will hold firmly to my duty as a subject and serve the celestial dynasty above.

sentences.zh: 若曰稍易初心，輒萌異志，豈獨不遵於祖禰，實當受譴於神明。

translations.literal: If one says he should slightly change his original heart and readily harbor a different intent, would he not only fail to follow his ancestors, but truly deserve punishment from the spirits?
translations.idiomatic: Should I ever change my heart or harbor disloyal intent, I would offend not only my ancestors but the spirits themselves.

sentences.zh: 方主一國之生靈，遐賴九天之覆燾。

translations.literal: He is just then presiding over the living beings of one state and from afar relies on the covering radiance of the Nine Heavens.
translations.idiomatic: I now govern the people of my state and look to Your Majesty's heaven-spanning protection from afar.

sentences.zh: 況陛下懷柔義廣，煦嫗仁深，必假清光，更逾曩日。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty's cherishing gentleness and righteousness are broad, and your nurturing kindness is deep; he must borrow your clear radiance, surpassing former days even more.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's kindness and righteousness are boundless, your nurturing grace profound; I must rely on your enlightened favor more than ever before.

sentences.zh: 遠憑帝力，下撫舊邦，克獲宴安，得從康泰。

translations.literal: From afar relying on imperial strength, below comforting his old domain, he can obtain repose in peace and follow prosperity and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Leaning on your imperial power from afar, I shall govern my old domain below and hope to secure peace and prosperity for my people.

sentences.zh: 然所慮者，吳越國鄰於弊土，近似深仇，猶恐輒向封疆，或生紛擾。

translations.literal: Yet what he worries about is that the state of Wuyue borders his weakened territory, is close and like a deep enemy; he still fears they may readily move against his borders and produce strife and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I worry that Wuyue, our neighbor and ancient enemy, may yet raid my borders and stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 臣即自嚴部曲，終不先有侵漁，免結釁嫌，撓幹旒扆。

translations.literal: Your subject will himself strictly discipline his troops and in the end not first make encroachments or depredations, to avoid forming causes of quarrel and disturbing Your Majesty's imperial canopy and throne screen.
translations.idiomatic: I shall discipline my troops strictly and never strike first, lest border quarrels trouble Your Majesty's court.

sentences.zh: 仍慮巧肆如簧之舌，仰成投杼之疑，曲構異端，潛行詭道。

translations.literal: He still fears clever tongues wagging like reed-pipes, looking up to create the suspicion of casting away the shuttle, twisting and fabricating strange charges, and secretly practicing deceitful ways.
translations.idiomatic: I still fear that clever tongues may slander me to Your Majesty, as in the tale of the mother who cast away her shuttle, weaving false charges and secret intrigues.

sentences.zh: 願回鑒燭，顯諭是非，庶使遠臣得安危懇。

translations.literal: He wishes Your Majesty to turn back your mirror and candle, clearly instructing right and wrong, so that this distant subject may obtain his earnest plea for safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to look clearly upon truth and falsehood and make plain who is right, so that your distant subject may know whether he stands in safety or peril.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔答焉。

translations.literal: Taizu issued an edict in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu issued an edict in reply.

sentences.zh: 自景畫江內附，周世宗貽書於景，至是，因煜之立，始下詔而不名。

translations.literal: From the time Jing drew the river as border and submitted inward, Zhou Shizong sent letters to Jing; at this point, because of Yu's accession, edicts were first issued without using his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jing had accepted the Yangzi as border and submitted, Zhou Shizong had addressed him by letter; only now, with Yu's accession, did Song begin to issue edicts without naming him personally.

sentences.zh: 會昭憲太后葬，煜遣戶部侍郎韓熙載、太府卿田霖來貢。

translations.literal: When the Zhaoxian Empress Dowager was buried, Yu sent his Vice Minister of Revenue Han Xizai and Grand Storekeeper Tian Lin to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhaoxian Empress Dowager was buried, Yu sent Vice Minister of Revenue Han Xizai and Grand Storekeeper Tian Lin with tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔煜應朝廷橫海、飛江、水鬥、懷順諸軍親屬有在江表者，悉遣令渡江。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered Yu to respond to the court: among the kin of the armies of Henghai, Feijiang, Shuidou, and Huaishun, any who were south of the Yangzi were all to be sent to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict required Yu to send across the river all relatives of Song troops in the Henghai, Feijiang, Shuidou, and Huaishun armies who were still living south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 煜每聞朝廷出師克捷及嘉慶之事，必遣使犒師修貢。

translations.literal: Whenever Yu heard of the court's dispatch of armies achieving victory and of celebratory occasions, he invariably sent envoys to reward the troops and present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Li Yu heard that Song armies had won a campaign or that the court was celebrating a joyous occasion, he always sent envoys to reward the troops and renew his tribute.

sentences.zh: 其大慶，即更以買宴為名，別奉珍玩為獻。

translations.literal: For great celebrations, he would further take the name of purchasing the banquet and separately present rare curios as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On major celebrations he would additionally send tribute under the rubric of purchasing the imperial banquet, separately offering rare treasures as gifts.

sentences.zh: 吉凶大禮，皆別修貢助。

translations.literal: For major ceremonies of fortune or misfortune, he would separately send tribute as assistance.
translations.idiomatic: For major ceremonies of joy or mourning he would likewise send separate tribute offerings.

sentences.zh: 煜有母妻之喪，亦遣使往吊。

translations.literal: When Yu had mourning for his mother or wife, [the court] also sent envoys to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu mourned the death of his mother or wife, the Song court also sent envoys to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，煜上表乞呼名，詔不許。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande, Yu submitted a memorial requesting to be addressed by name; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qiande, Li Yu submitted a memorial asking that imperial edicts address him by name; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 二年，又詔江北，許諸州民及諸監鹽亭戶緣江采捕及過江貿易。

translations.literal: In the second year, another edict [addressed] north of the Yangzi, permitting commoners of the various prefectures and salt-yard households of the various salt commissions to gather and fish along the river and to cross the river to trade.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year another edict permitted people north of the Yangzi—commoners of the various prefectures and salt-yard households attached to the salt commissions—to gather and fish along the river and to cross the river to trade.

sentences.zh: 先是，江北置榷場，禁商人渡江及百姓緣江樵采。

translations.literal: Earlier, north of the Yangzi monopoly markets had been established, prohibiting merchants from crossing the river and commoners from gathering firewood along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Song had established monopoly markets north of the Yangzi and forbidden merchants to cross the river or commoners to gather firewood along its banks.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以江南薦饑，特弛其禁。

translations.literal: That year, because Jiangnan suffered repeated famine, the prohibition was specially relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: That year, because Jiangnan was suffering repeated famine, the restriction was specially lifted.

sentences.zh: 三年，獻銀二萬兩、金銀龍鳳茶酒器數百事。

translations.literal: In the third year, he presented twenty thousand taels of silver and over a hundred items of gold and silver dragon-phoenix tea and wine vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he presented twenty thousand taels of silver and more than a hundred gold and silver tea and wine vessels decorated with dragons and phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，又以占城、闍婆、大食國所送禮物來上，又遣弟從謙奉珍寶器用金帛為貢，且買宴，其數皆倍於前。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, he again presented upward the gifts sent by Champa, Java, and the Dashi state, and further sent his younger brother Congqian bearing precious treasures, utensils, gold, and silk as tribute, and also for purchasing the banquet; the quantities were all double those of before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao he also forwarded upward tribute gifts sent by Champa, Java, and the Arab lands, and sent his younger brother Congqian with precious treasures, utensils, gold, and silk as tribute—including banquet tribute—and every amount was twice what he had sent before.

sentences.zh: 是冬，以將郊祀，又遣弟從善來貢。

translations.literal: That winter, because the court was about to perform suburban sacrifices, he again sent his younger brother Congshan to come as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, as the court was preparing for the suburban sacrifice, he again sent his younger brother Congshan with tribute.

sentences.zh: 會嶺南平，煜懼，上表，遂改唐國主為江南國主，唐國印為江南國印。

translations.literal: When Lingnan was pacified, Yu grew fearful and submitted a memorial; [the court] thereupon changed Prince of Tang to Prince of Jiangnan, and the seal of Tang to the seal of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingnan was pacified, Li Yu grew alarmed and submitted a memorial; the court thereupon changed his title from Prince of Tang to Prince of Jiangnan and replaced the seal of Tang with the seal of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 又上表請所賜詔呼名，許之。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial requesting that edicts granted to him address him by name; this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial asking that edicts addressed to him use his personal name, and this was granted.

sentences.zh: 煜又貶損制度，下書稱教；

translations.literal: Yu also reduced his institutions, calling his written orders "instructions";
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu further scaled back his institutions, styling his written orders "instructions";

sentences.zh: 改中書門下省為左右內史府，尚書省為司會府，御史臺為司憲府，翰林為文館，樞密院為光政院；

translations.literal: changing the Secretariat-Chancellery into the Left and Right Inner Secretariat offices, the Department of State Affairs into the Office of Accounts, the Censorate into the Office of Law, the Hanlin Academy into the Literary Institute, and the Bureau of Military Affairs into the Bureau of Glorious Governance;
translations.idiomatic: renaming the Secretariat-Chancellery the Left and Right Inner Secretariat, the Department of State Affairs the Office of Accounts, the Censorate the Office of Law, the Hanlin Academy the Literary Institute, and the Bureau of Military Affairs the Bureau of Glorious Governance;

sentences.zh: 降封諸王為國公，官號多所改易。

translations.literal: demoting all princes to state dukes, with many official titles changed.
translations.idiomatic: demoting all princes to state dukes and changing many official titles.

sentences.zh: 五年，長春節，別貢錢三十萬，遂以為常。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on the Longevity Festival, he separately presented tribute of three hundred thousand [strings of cash]; this then became the regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on his birthday festival, he sent a separate tribute of three hundred thousand strings of cash, and this thereafter became customary.

sentences.zh: 太祖以從善為泰寧軍節度，賜第留京師。

translations.literal: The Emperor Taizu appointed Congshan military commissioner of the Taining Army, granted him a residence, and kept him in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu appointed Congshan military commissioner of the Taining Army, granted him a residence, and kept him in the capital.

sentences.zh: 是歲，煜又貢米麥二十萬石。

translations.literal: That year, Yu again presented two hundred thousand shi of rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Yu also sent two hundred thousand shi of rice and wheat as tribute.

sentences.zh: 雖外示畏服，修藩臣之禮，而內實繕甲募兵，潛為戰備。

translations.literal: Although outwardly showing fear and submission, observing the rites of a vassal, inwardly he was actually repairing armor, recruiting troops, and secretly preparing for war.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he showed fear and performed every rite of a vassal, but inwardly he repaired armor, recruited troops, and secretly prepared for war.

sentences.zh: 太祖慮其難製，令從善諭旨於煜，使來朝，煜但奉方物為貢。

translations.literal: The Emperor Taizu, fearing he would be hard to control, had Congshan convey the imperial will to Yu, instructing him to come to court; Yu only offered local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, fearing that Li Yu would prove hard to control, had Congshan convey the imperial command that he come to court; Li Yu responded only by sending local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 六年，賜米麥十萬斛，振其饑民。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, [the court] granted one hundred thousand hu of rice and wheat to relieve his famine-stricken people.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the court granted one hundred thousand hu of rice and wheat to relieve his famine-stricken people.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，遂詔煜赴闕，煜稱疾不奉詔。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year, an edict finally summoned Yu to the palace; Yu claimed illness and did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year an edict summoned Li Yu to court; he pleaded illness and refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 冬，乃興師致討，以宣徽南院使、義成軍節度曹彬為升州西南面行營都部署，山南東道節度潘美為都監。

translations.literal: In winter, [the court] raised an army to punish him, appointing Xuannui Southern Court commissioner and Yicheng Army military commissioner Cao Bin as overall commander of the mobile camp on the southwest of Sheng Prefecture, and Shannan East Circuit military commissioner Pan Mei as overall supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the court raised an army to punish him, appointing Xuannui Southern Court commissioner and Yicheng Army military commissioner Cao Bin overall commander of the mobile camp southwest of Sheng Prefecture, with Shannan East Circuit military commissioner Pan Mei as overall supervisor.

sentences.zh: 煜初聞大兵將舉，甚惶懼，遣其弟從鎰及潘慎修來買宴，貢絹二十萬匹、茶二十萬斤及金銀器用、乘輿服物等。

translations.literal: When Yu first heard that a great army was about to march, he was greatly alarmed and sent his younger brother Congyi and Pan Shenxiu to purchase the banquet, presenting tribute of two hundred thousand bolts of silk, two hundred thousand jin of tea, and gold and silver utensils, imperial carriage garments, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu first heard that a great army was about to march, he was deeply alarmed and sent his younger brother Congyi and Pan Shenxiu with banquet tribute, offering two hundred thousand bolts of silk, two hundred thousand jin of tea, and gold and silver utensils, imperial carriage garments, and the like.

sentences.zh: 及至，遂留於別館。

translations.literal: When they arrived, they were detained at a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, the court detained them at a separate lodge.

sentences.zh: 王師克池州，又破其眾二萬於采石磯，擒其龍驤都虞候楊收等，獲馬三百匹。

translations.literal: The imperial army captured Chizhou, then defeated twenty thousand of his troops at Caishi Ji, capturing his Longxiang deputy commander-in-chief Yang Shou and others, and obtaining three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army captured Chizhou, then routed twenty thousand of his men at Caishi Ji, capturing his Longxiang deputy commander Yang Shou and others and seizing three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 江表無戰馬，朝廷歲賜之。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi had no war horses; the court granted them annually.
translations.idiomatic: The region south of the Yangzi had no war horses; the Song court granted them every year.

sentences.zh: 及是所獲，觀其印文，皆歲賜之馬也。

translations.literal: When these captured horses were examined, their seal marks showed they were all horses granted annually [by the court].
translations.idiomatic: When these captured horses were examined, their seal marks showed that they were all horses the court had granted year by year.

sentences.zh: 初，將有事江表，江南進士樊若水詣闕獻策，請造浮梁以濟師。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the court was planning action against the region south of the Yangzi, Jiangnan jinshi Fan Ruoshui came to the capital to offer a plan, requesting the construction of a floating bridge to ferry the army across.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the court was planning action south of the Yangzi, Jiangnan jinshi Fan Ruoshui came to court with a plan proposing a floating bridge to ferry the army across.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣高品石全振往荊湖造黃黑龍船數千艘，又以大艦載巨竹縆，自荊渚而下。

translations.literal: The Emperor Taizu sent the senior artisan Shi Quanzhen to Jinghu to build several thousand yellow and black dragon boats, and also had large ships carry huge bamboo cables downstream from Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent the senior artisan Shi Quanzhen to Jinghu to build several thousand yellow and black dragon boats, and had large ships carry huge bamboo cables downstream from Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及命曹彬等出師，乃遣八作使郝守濬等率丁匠營之。

translations.literal: When Cao Bin and others were ordered to march, [the court] sent Directorate of Palace Buildings commissioner Hao Shoujun and others to lead laborers and artisans to construct it.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Bin and the others were ordered to march, the court sent Directorate of Palace Buildings commissioner Hao Shoujun and others to lead laborers and artisans in building it.

sentences.zh: 議者以為古未有作浮梁渡大江者，恐不能就。

translations.literal: Critics thought that since antiquity no one had built a floating bridge to cross the great river, and feared it could not be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that since antiquity no one had built a floating bridge to cross the great river, and they doubted it could be done.

sentences.zh: 乃先試於石牌口，移置采石，三日而成，渡江若履平地。

translations.literal: They first tested it at Shipai Kou, then moved it to Caishi; it was completed in three days, and crossing the river was like walking on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: They first tested it at Shipai Kou, then moved it to Caishi; it was finished in three days, and crossing the river was like walking on level ground.

sentences.zh: 煜初聞朝廷作浮梁，語其臣張洎，洎對曰：「載籍已來，長江無為梁之事。

translations.literal: When Yu first heard the court was building a floating bridge, he spoke to his minister Zhang Bi; Bi replied: "Since records have been kept, there has never been building a bridge across the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu first heard that the court was building a floating bridge, he spoke to his minister Zhang Bi; Bi replied: "Since records have been kept, no one has ever bridged the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 」煜曰：「吾亦以為兒戲耳。」

translations.literal: " Yu said: "I too thought it was child's play."
translations.idiomatic: " Li Yu said: "I too considered it mere child's play."

sentences.zh: 王師渡江，煜委兵柄於皇甫繼勳，委機事於陳喬、張洎，又以徐溫諸孫元楀等為傳詔，每軍書告急，多不時通。

translations.literal: When the imperial army crossed the river, Yu entrusted military authority to Huangfu Jixun, entrusted affairs of state to Chen Qiao and Zhang Bi, and also made Xu Wen's grandsons Yuanyu and others transmit imperial edicts; whenever urgent military reports arrived, they were often not relayed in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army crossed the river, Li Yu entrusted military command to Huangfu Jixun and state affairs to Chen Qiao and Zhang Bi; he also made Xu Wen's grandsons Yuanyu and others relay edicts, and urgent military reports were often not passed on in time.

sentences.zh: 八年春，王師傅城下，煜猶不知。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, the imperial army encamped beneath the city walls, yet Yu still did not know.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year the imperial army had encamped beneath the city walls, yet Li Yu still did not know.

sentences.zh: 一日登城，見列柵於外，旌旗遍野，始大懼，知為近習所蔽，遂殺繼勳。

translations.literal: One day he ascended the wall and saw palisades arrayed outside and banners filling the plain; he then grew greatly terrified, realizing he had been deceived by his close attendants, and had Jixun killed.
translations.idiomatic: One day he climbed the wall and saw palisades arrayed outside and banners filling the plain; only then was he deeply terrified. Realizing he had been deceived by his close attendants, he had Jixun executed.

sentences.zh: 召朱令贇於上江，令連巨筏載甲士數萬人順流而下，將斷浮梁，未至，為劉遇所破。

translations.literal: He summoned Zhu Lingyun from upstream and ordered him to link giant rafts carrying tens of thousands of armored soldiers to float downstream, intending to sever the floating bridge; before he arrived, he was defeated by Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Zhu Lingyun from upstream and ordered him to link giant rafts carrying tens of thousands of armored men to float downstream and cut the floating bridge; before he arrived he was defeated by Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 又募勇士五千餘人謀襲官軍，皆素不習戰，以暮夜人秉一炬來攻襲北砦。

translations.literal: He also recruited over five thousand brave men to plan a raid on the government army; they were all untrained in warfare, and at night each man carrying a torch came to attack the northern camp.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited more than five thousand brave men to raid the government army; they were wholly untrained in warfare, and at night each man carrying a torch came to attack the northern camp.

sentences.zh: 宋師縱其至，擊之，殲焉。

translations.literal: The Song army let them approach, then struck and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Song army let them come close, then struck and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 獲其將帥，悉佩印符。

translations.literal: Those captured among their generals and commanders all wore official seals and tally tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Among the captured commanders, all wore official seals and tally tokens.

sentences.zh: 初，彬之南征也，太祖親諭之曰：「卿至彼慎勿暴略，可示以兵威，俾自歸順，不必急攻。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bin was setting out on the southern campaign, the Emperor Taizu personally instructed him: "When you arrive there, be careful not to plunder and ravage; you may display military might so that they surrender of their own accord — there is no need to press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cao Bin set out on the southern campaign, Taizu personally instructed him: "When you arrive there, take care not to plunder; show your military might so that they surrender of their own accord—there is no need to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 」及彬軍圍城，又命左拾遺、知制誥李穆送從鎰還本國，諭以手詔，促其降。

translations.literal: " When Bin's army besieged the city, [the Emperor] again ordered Left Reminder and Drafting Drafter Li Mu to escort Congyi back to his state, conveying a handwritten edict urging his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " When Cao Bin's army besieged the city, the court again ordered Left Reminder and Drafting Drafter Li Mu to escort Congyi back to his country, conveying a handwritten edict urging surrender.

sentences.zh: 會潤州平，煜危迫甚，遣其臣徐鉉、周惟簡奉方物來貢，手書奏目以來，哀懇求罷兵，太祖不許。

translations.literal: When Runzhou was pacified, Yu was in dire straits; he sent his ministers Xu Xuan and Zhou Weijian bearing local products as tribute, with a handwritten memorial listing [items] sent, pleading piteously to halt the army; the Emperor Taizu refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Runzhou fell, Li Yu was in desperate straits; he sent his ministers Xu Xuan and Zhou Weijian with local products as tribute and a handwritten memorial listing what was sent, pleading piteously for the army to be withdrawn; Taizu refused.

sentences.zh: 俄復遣鉉等入貢，仍乞緩師，又不答，但厚賜遣之。

translations.literal: Soon he again sent Xuan and others with tribute, still begging to slow the army; again there was no reply, but they were generously rewarded and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent Xu Xuan and the others with tribute again, still begging that the advance be slowed; again there was no answer, but they were generously rewarded and sent away.

sentences.zh: 初，從鎰之還，詔諸將罷攻城，而煜終惑左右之言，猶豫不決，遂詔進兵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Congyi returned, an edict ordered the generals to cease the siege; but Yu, finally confused by the words of those around him, hesitated and could not decide, whereupon an edict ordered the advance of troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Congyi returned, an edict had ordered the generals to halt the siege, but Li Yu, swayed to the end by those around him, hesitated and could not decide; an edict then ordered the advance to resume.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，城陷，曹彬等駐兵於宮門，煜率其近臣迎拜於門。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year, the city fell; Cao Bin and others stationed troops at the palace gate, and Yu led his close ministers to welcome and bow at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eighth year the city fell; Cao Bin and the others stationed troops at the palace gate, and Li Yu led his close ministers out to welcome them and bow at the gate.

sentences.zh: 彬等上露布，以煜並其宰相湯悅等四十五人上獻。

translations.literal: Bin and others submitted a battle report, presenting Yu together with his chancellor Tang Yue and forty-five others upward.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Bin and the others submitted a victory bulletin, presenting Li Yu together with his chancellor Tang Yue and forty-five others to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太祖禦明德樓，以煜嘗奉正朔，詔有司勿宣露布，止令煜等白衣紗帽至樓下待罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor Taizu ascended Mingde Tower; because Yu had once observed the imperial calendar, he ordered the officials not to proclaim the battle report, only requiring Yu and the others to come in white robes and gauze caps to await judgment beneath the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu ascended Mingde Tower; because Li Yu had once observed the Song calendar, he ordered the officials not to proclaim the victory bulletin and required Li Yu and the others to come in white robes and gauze caps to await judgment beneath the tower.

sentences.zh: 詔並釋之，賜冠帶、器幣、鞍馬有差。

translations.literal: An edict released them all, granting caps and belts, vessels and gifts, saddles and horses in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: An edict released them all and granted caps and belts, vessels and gifts, saddles and horses in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict was issued, stating:
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued, stating:

sentences.zh: 上天之德本於好生，為君之心貴乎含垢。

translations.literal: The virtue of Heaven above is rooted in cherishing life; the mind of a ruler values bearing with stains.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's virtue is rooted in cherishing life; a ruler's heart is prized for bearing with stains.

sentences.zh: 自亂離之雲瘼，致跨據之相承，諭文告而弗賓，申吊伐而斯在。

translations.literal: Since the afflictions of turmoil and separation, leading to successive usurpations across territories, though written proclamations were issued yet he did not come as guest, the appeal to punitive expedition was therefore at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Since the afflictions of turmoil and separation gave rise to successive usurpations across the land, though written proclamations were issued he did not come as a guest, and the call to punitive expedition was therefore at hand.

sentences.zh: 慶茲混一，加以寵綏。

translations.literal: Let us rejoice in this unification and add favor and reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: Let us rejoice in this unification and extend favor and reassurance.

sentences.zh: 江南偽主李煜，承奕世之遺基，據偏方而竊號。

translations.literal: The false ruler of Jiangnan, Li Yu, inherited the legacy of generations, occupied a remote corner and usurped a title.
translations.idiomatic: The false ruler of Jiangnan, Li Yu, inherited a legacy of generations, occupied a remote corner, and usurped a title.

sentences.zh: 惟乃先父早荷朝恩，當爾襲位之初，未嘗稟命。

translations.literal: Yet his late father early received court favor; when he first succeeded to the throne, he never reported for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his late father had early received the court's favor; when he first succeeded to the throne, he never reported for approval.

sentences.zh: 朕方示以寬大，每為含容。

translations.literal: I showed him magnanimity and repeatedly bore with him.
translations.idiomatic: I showed him magnanimity and repeatedly bore with him.

sentences.zh: 雖陳內附之言，罔效駿奔之禮，聚兵峻壘，包蓄日彰。

translations.literal: Although he professed submission, he failed to perform the rite of urgent attendance; gathering troops and fortifying ramparts, his hidden designs grew daily apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Although he professed submission, he failed to perform the rite of urgent attendance; gathering troops and fortifying ramparts, his hidden designs grew daily clearer.

sentences.zh: 朕欲全彼始終，去其疑間，雖頒召節，亦冀來朝，庶成玉帛之儀，豈願干戈之役。

translations.literal: I wished to preserve him from beginning to end and remove his suspicions; though summons were issued, I also hoped he would come to court, that the rites of tribute might be fulfilled — who would wish for the labor of arms?
translations.idiomatic: I wished to preserve him from beginning to end and remove his suspicions; though summons were issued, I also hoped he would come to court so that the rites of tribute might be fulfilled—who would wish for the labor of arms?

sentences.zh: 蹇然弗顧，潛蓄陰謀。

translations.literal: He stubbornly paid no heed and secretly harbored treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: He stubbornly paid no heed and secretly harbored treacherous designs.

sentences.zh: 勞銳旅以徂征，傅孤城而問罪。

translations.literal: I had to weary sharp troops on punitive march and press a lone city to account for its crimes.
translations.idiomatic: I had to weary sharp troops on punitive march and press a lone city to account for its crimes.

sentences.zh: 洎聞危迫，累示招攜，何迷復之不悛，果覆亡之自掇。

translations.literal: When he heard of his peril, repeated offers of clemency were shown — why would he not turn from his error? In the end he brought ruin upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of his peril, repeated offers of clemency were shown—why would he not turn from his error? In the end he brought ruin upon himself.

sentences.zh: 昔者唐堯光宅，非無丹浦之師；

translations.literal: In ancient times, when Tang Yao illuminated the realm, there was not lacking the army at Red Bank;
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, when Tang Yao illuminated the realm, there was not lacking the army at Red Bank;

sentences.zh: 夏禹泣辜，不赦防風之罪。

translations.literal: When Xia Yu wept over the guilty, he did not pardon the crime of Fangfeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Yu wept over the guilty, he did not pardon the crime of Fangfeng.

sentences.zh: 稽諸古典，諒有明刑。

translations.literal: Consulting the ancient classics, surely there are clear punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting the ancient classics, surely there are clear punishments.

sentences.zh: 朕以道在包荒，恩推惡殺。

translations.literal: I, holding that the Way lies in encompassing the wild, extend grace and abhor killing.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the Way lies in encompassing the wild, and I extend grace and abhor killing.

sentences.zh: 在昔騾車出蜀，青蓋辭吳，彼皆閏位之降君，不預中朝之正朔，及頒爵命，方列公侯。

translations.literal: In former times the mule cart departed Shu and the green-canopied carriage left Wu — those were all abdicated rulers of intercalary reigns, who did not observe the imperial calendar of the central court; only when titles were granted did they rank as dukes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: In former times the mule cart departed Shu and the green-canopied carriage left Wu—those were all abdicated rulers of intercalary reigns who did not observe the central court's calendar; only when titles were granted did they rank as dukes and marquises.

sentences.zh: 爾實為外臣，戾我恩德，比禪與皓，又非其倫。

translations.literal: You were in truth an outer minister who violated my grace and virtue — compared with Chang and Hao, you are not of their class.
translations.idiomatic: You were in truth an outer minister who violated my grace and virtue; compared with Meng Chang and Liu Chang, you are not of their class.

sentences.zh: 特升拱極之班，賜以列侯之號，式優待遇，盡舍尤違。

translations.literal: Specially elevated to the ranks beside the Pole Star, granted the title of a ranked marquis — thus generously treated, all your grave transgressions are set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Specially elevated to the ranks beside the Pole Star and granted the title of a ranked marquis, you are thus generously treated and all your grave transgressions are set aside.

sentences.zh: 可光祿大夫、檢校太傅、右千牛衛上將軍，仍封違命侯。

translations.literal: Appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Grand Mentor, Senior General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and still enfeoffed as Marquis of Disobedience to Orders.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Grand Mentor, Senior General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and enfeoffed as Marquis Who Disobeyed Orders.

sentences.zh: 召升殿撫問。

translations.literal: He was summoned to ascend the hall and was comfortingly questioned.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to ascend the hall and was comfortingly questioned.

sentences.zh: 妻周氏封鄭國夫人，又以其子神武右廂都指揮使仲寓為左千牛衛大將軍，弟宣州節度使從鎰為左領軍衛大將軍，江州節度使從謙為右領軍衛大將軍，神武統軍從度為左監門衛大將軍，神武左廂都指揮使從信為右監門衛大將軍，侄戶部尚書仲遠為右驍衛將軍，刑部尚書仲興為右武衛將軍，禮部尚書仲偉為右屯衛將軍，宗正卿季操為左武衛將軍，殿中監仲康為右領衛將軍，殿中少監仲宣為監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Zhou was enfeoffed as Lady of Zheng; his son Zhongyu, commander of the right division of the Shenwu Army, was made Senior General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard; his younger brother Congyi, military commissioner of Xuanzhou, was made Senior General of the Left Army Guard; Congqian, military commissioner of Jiangzhou, was made Senior General of the Right Army Guard; Congdu, overall commander of the Shenwu Army, was made Senior General of the Left Gate Guard; Congxin, commander of the left division of the Shenwu Army, was made Senior General of the Right Gate Guard; his nephew Zhongyuan, Minister of Revenue, was made General of the Right Xiaowei Guard; Zhongxing, Minister of Justice, was made General of the Right Wuwei Guard; Zhongwei, Minister of Rites, was made General of the Right Tunwei Guard; Jicao, Director of the Imperial Clan, was made General of the Left Wuwei Guard; Zhongkang, Director of the Palace Bureau, was made General of the Right Ling Guard; Zhongxuan, Vice Director of the Palace Bureau, was made General of the Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Zhou was enfeoffed as Lady of Zheng; his son Zhongyu, commander of the right division of the Shenwu Army, was made Senior General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard; his younger brother Congyi, military commissioner of Xuanzhou, was made Senior General of the Left Army Guard; Congqian, military commissioner of Jiangzhou, was made Senior General of the Right Army Guard; Congdu, overall commander of the Shenwu Army, was made Senior General of the Left Gate Guard; Congxin, commander of the left division of the Shenwu Army, was made Senior General of the Right Gate Guard; his nephew Zhongyuan, Minister of Revenue, was made General of the Right Xiaowei Guard; Zhongxing, Minister of Justice, was made General of the Right Wuwei Guard; Zhongwei, Minister of Rites, was made General of the Right Tunwei Guard; Jicao, Director of the Imperial Clan, was made General of the Left Wuwei Guard; Zhongkang, Director of the Palace Bureau, was made General of the Right Ling Guard; and Zhongxuan, Vice Director of the Palace Bureau, was made General of the Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 仍賜其弟侄宅各一區。

translations.literal: Each of his younger brothers and nephews was also granted one residence.
translations.idiomatic: Each of his younger brothers and nephews was also granted a residence.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，始去違命侯，加特進，封隴西郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, the title Marquis of Disobedience to Orders was first removed; he was given the special advancement rank and enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, the title Marquis Who Disobeyed Orders was removed; he was given the special advancement rank and enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，煜自言其貧，詔增給月奉，仍賜錢三百萬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, Yu said he was poor; an edict increased his monthly stipend and also granted three million cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, Li Yu said he was poor; an edict increased his monthly stipend and also granted three million cash.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗幸崇文院觀書，召煜及劉鋹，令縱觀，謂煜曰：「聞卿在江南好讀書，此簡策多卿之舊物，歸朝來頗讀書否？

translations.literal: The Emperor Taizong once visited the Hall of Literary Glory to view books; he summoned Yu and Liu Chang and allowed them to browse freely, saying to Yu: "I hear that in Jiangnan you loved to read — many of these texts were once yours. Since coming to court, have you read much?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once visited the Hall of Literary Glory to view books; he summoned Li Yu and Liu Chang and allowed them to browse freely, saying to Li Yu: "I hear that in Jiangnan you loved to read—many of these texts were once yours. Since coming to court, have you read much?

sentences.zh: 」煜頓首謝。

translations.literal: " Yu bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Yu bowed his head in thanks.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, he died, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year he died, aged forty-two.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈太師，追封吳王。

translations.literal: Court mourning was suspended for three days; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and retroactively enfeoffed as King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning was suspended for three days; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and retroactively enfeoffed as King of Wu.

sentences.zh: 先是，江南自後漢以來，民間有服玩侈靡者，人詢之，必對曰：「此物屬趙寶子。

translations.literal: Earlier, since Later Han times in Jiangnan, when people had lavish clothing and ornaments and were asked about them, they would invariably answer: "These things belong to Zhao Baozi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, since Later Han times in Jiangnan, when people had lavish clothing and ornaments and were asked about them, they would invariably answer: "These things belong to Zhao Baozi.

sentences.zh: 」又煜之妓妾嘗染碧，經夕未收，會露下，其色愈鮮明，煜愛之。

translations.literal: " Also, one of Yu's concubines once dyed fabric azure; it was not taken in overnight, and when dew fell upon it the color grew brighter; Yu was delighted.
translations.idiomatic: " Also, one of Li Yu's concubines once dyed fabric azure; it was not taken in overnight, and when dew fell upon it the color grew brighter; Li Yu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 自是宮中競收露水，染碧以衣之，謂之「天水碧」。

translations.literal: From then on the palace competed to collect dew, dyeing fabric azure to make clothing, calling it "Heaven-Water Azure."
translations.idiomatic: From then on the palace women competed to collect dew, dye fabric azure for clothing, and call it "Heaven-Water Azure."

sentences.zh: 及江南滅，方悟「趙」，國姓也；

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was destroyed, they finally understood that "Zhao" was the imperial surname;
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan fell, people finally understood that "Zhao" was the Song imperial surname;

sentences.zh: 「寶」，年號也；

translations.literal: "Bao" was an era name;
translations.idiomatic: "Bao" was an era name;

sentences.zh: 「天水」，趙之望也。

translations.literal: "Heaven-Water" was the ancestral seat of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven-Water" was the ancestral seat of the Zhao house.

sentences.zh: 從善字子師，偽封鄭王，累遷太尉、中書令，後降封南楚國公。

translations.literal: Congshan, courtesy name Zishi, was falsely enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng, repeatedly promoted to Grand Marshal and Palace Secretariat Director, and later demoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Southern Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Congshan, courtesy name Zishi, had been enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng, rose through the posts of Grand Marshal and Palace Secretariat Director, and was later demoted to Duke of Southern Chu.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年春，奉方物來貢，授泰寧軍節度、兗海沂等州觀察等使，留京師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Kaibao, he presented local products as tribute, was appointed military commissioner of the Taining Army and observation commissioner of Yan, Hai, Yi, and other prefectures, and was kept in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year of Kaibao he came with local products as tribute, was appointed military commissioner of the Taining Army and observation commissioner of Yan, Hai, Yi, and other prefectures, and was kept in the capital.

sentences.zh: 時太祖平劉鋹，將召煜入朝，故授從善節制，仍賜汴陽坊甲第一區。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor Taizu had pacified Liu Chang and was about to summon Yu to court; therefore he appointed Congshan as military commissioner and also granted him the foremost residence in Bianyang Ward.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Taizu had pacified Liu Chang and was about to summon Li Yu to court; he therefore appointed Congshan as military commissioner and granted him the foremost residence in Bianyang Ward.

sentences.zh: 煜手疏求遣從善歸國，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Yu wrote a personal memorial requesting that Congshan be sent back to his country; a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu wrote a personal memorial asking that Congshan be sent home; a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 七年，推恩將佐，以掌書記江直木為司門員外郎、同判兗州，衙內都指揮使兼左都押衙崔光習為右千牛衛將軍，衙內都虞候兼右都押衙子再興為右千牛衛中郎將，並同正。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, extending favor to his officers and aides, [the court] appointed secretary Jiang Zhimu as Vice Director of the Gate Office and co-administrator of Yan Prefecture, palace inner overall commander and left chief adjutant Cui Guangxi as General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, palace inner deputy commander-in-chief and right chief adjutant Zi Zaixing as Captain of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard — all with regular appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, extending favor to his officers and aides, the court appointed secretary Jiang Zhimu Vice Director of the Gate Office and co-administrator of Yan Prefecture, palace inner overall commander and left chief adjutant Cui Guangxi General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and palace inner deputy commander and right chief adjutant Zi Zaixing Captain of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard—all with regular appointments.

sentences.zh: 又封從善母淩氏吳國太夫人。

translations.literal: Congshan's mother Lady Ling was also enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Congshan's mother Lady Ling was also enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Wu.

sentences.zh: 江南平，改右神武大將軍。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, he was changed to Senior General of the Right Shenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan fell, he was made Senior General of the Right Shenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，再遷右千牛衛上將軍，出為通許監軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, he was again promoted to Senior General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and sent out as military supervisor of Tongxu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongxi he was again promoted to Senior General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and sent out as military supervisor of Tongxu.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he died, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died, aged forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子仲翊，大中祥符初，賜同進士出身。

translations.literal: His son Zhongyi, at the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, was granted the status of one who had passed the jinshi examination with honors.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongyi, at the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, was granted jinshi status with honors.

sentences.zh: 二年，復召試，除楚州推官，累遷殿中丞，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was again summoned for examination, appointed push official of Chuzhou, repeatedly promoted to Palace Aide, and dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was again summoned for examination, appointed legal officer of Chuzhou, rose to Palace Aide, and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 次子仲猷，景德中，特錄為三班借職。

translations.literal: His second son Zhongyou, during the Jingde era, was specially enrolled as a probationary officer of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Zhongyou, during the Jingde era, was specially enrolled as a probationary officer of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 從誧本名從謙，偽封吉王，後降封鄂國公。
