translations.literal: Congbu's original name was Congqian; he was falsely enfeoffed as Prince of Ji, and later demoted and enfeoffed as Duke of E.
translations.idiomatic: Congbu's original name was Congqian; he had been enfeoffed as Prince of Ji and was later demoted to Duke of E.

sentences.zh: 隨煜歸朝，為右領軍衛大將軍，遷右龍武大將軍，歷知隨、復、成三州。

translations.literal: Following Yu in submitting to the court, he was made Senior General of the Right Leading Army Guard, transferred to Senior General of the Right Longwu Army, and successively administered the three prefectures of Sui, Fu, and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Li Yu to submit to the court, was made Senior General of the Right Leading Army Guard, transferred to Senior General of the Right Longwu Army, and successively governed Sui, Fu, and Cheng prefectures.

sentences.zh: 上表改名。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting a change of name.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting a name change.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，上言貧不能自給，求外任。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua, he memorialized that he was too poor to support himself and requested an appointment outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua he memorialized that he was too poor to support himself and asked for a post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 以本官充武勝軍行軍司馬，月給奉錢三萬。

translations.literal: Retaining his original rank, he was appointed aide-de-camp on campaign of the Wusheng Army, with a monthly salary stipend of thirty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed, at his existing rank, aide-de-camp on campaign of the Wusheng Army, with a monthly stipend of thirty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 子仲偃，大中祥符八年，舉進士。

translations.literal: His son Zhongyan passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongyan passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 季操，從父弟偽江王逷之子也。

translations.literal: Jicao was the son of You, the false Prince of Jiang, who was his younger paternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Jicao was the son of You, the Prince of Jiang, who was his younger paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 從煜入朝，後為右神武將軍，累遷左衛大將軍，領康州刺史，出為單州都監。

translations.literal: Following Yu to court, he later became General of the Right Shenwu Army, was repeatedly promoted to Senior General of the Left Guard, concurrently served as prefect of Kangzhou, and was sent out as overall supervisor of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Li Yu to court, later became General of the Right Shenwu Army, rose to Senior General of the Left Guard, served concurrently as prefect of Kangzhou, and was sent out as overall supervisor of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷知淮陽漣水二軍、蔡舒二州。

translations.literal: He successively administered the two armies of Huaiyang and Lianshui and the two prefectures of Cai and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He successively governed the Huaiyang and Lianshui armies and Cai and Shu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died.

sentences.zh: 仲寓字叔章，少聰慧，能屬文，多才藝。

translations.literal: Zhongyu, courtesy name Shuzhang, was intelligent from youth, could compose prose, and had many talents and skills.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyu, courtesy name Shuzhang, was clever from youth, could write well, and had many talents.

sentences.zh: 偽封清源郡公，歸朝為千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was falsely enfeoffed as Duke of Qingyuan Commandery; after submitting to the court he became Senior General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He had been enfeoffed as Duke of Qingyuan Commandery; after submitting to the court he became Senior General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 煜卒，太宗賜仲寓積珍坊第一區、白金五千兩。

translations.literal: When Yu died, Taizong granted Zhongyu the foremost residence in Jizhen Ward and five thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu died, Emperor Taizong granted Zhongyu the foremost residence in Jizhen Ward and five thousand taels of white silver.

sentences.zh: 仲寓宗族百餘口，猶貧不能給，上書自陳。

translations.literal: More than a hundred members of Zhongyu's clan still could not be provided for and remained poor; he submitted a memorial stating his case.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred members of Zhongyu's clan still could not be supported and remained poor; he submitted a memorial explaining his situation.

sentences.zh: 太宗憐之，授郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Taizong took pity on him and appointed him prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong took pity on him and appointed him prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 在郡迨十年，為政寬簡，部內甚治。

translations.literal: He was in the prefecture for nearly ten years; his governance was lenient and simple, and the district was very well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the prefecture for nearly ten years with lenient and simple administration, and the district was very well ordered.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，卒，年三十七。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua, he died, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua he died, aged thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子正言，景德三年，特補供奉官。

translations.literal: His son Zhengyan, in the third year of Jingde, was specially appointed Attendant Officer.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengyan, in the third year of Jingde, was specially appointed Attendant Officer.

sentences.zh: 早卒無嗣，唯一女孤幼，真宗湣之，賜絹百匹、錢二百萬，以備聘財，仍遣內臣主其事。

translations.literal: He died young without heirs; he had only one daughter, orphaned and young. Zhenzong took pity on her, granted a hundred bolts of silk and two million cash as betrothal goods, and dispatched a palace eunuch to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He died young without heirs, leaving only one orphaned daughter. Zhenzong took pity on her, granted a hundred bolts of silk and two million cash for her betrothal, and sent a palace eunuch to oversee the arrangements.

sentences.zh: 煜有土田在常州，官為檢校。

translations.literal: Yu had land in Changzhou; the state served as trustee over it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu had land in Changzhou, which the state held in trust.

sentences.zh: 上聞其宗屬貧甚，命鬻其半，置資產以贍之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that his clansmen were extremely poor and ordered half of it sold and assets set aside to support them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard that his clansmen were extremely poor, he ordered half the land sold and the proceeds set aside to support them.

sentences.zh: 舒元，潁州沈丘人。

translations.literal: Shu Yuan was a native of Shenqiu in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Yuan was a native of Shenqiu in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻好學，與道士楊訥講習於嵩陽，通《左氏》及《公》、《穀》二傳。

translations.literal: From youth he was bold and unrestrained and loved learning; with the Daoist Yang Ne he studied at Songyang, mastering the Zuo Commentary and the Gong and Gu commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was bold and loved learning; with the Daoist Yang Ne he studied at Songyang and mastered the Zuo Commentary and the Gong and Gu commentaries.

sentences.zh: 與訥同詣河中謁李守貞，與語奇之，俱館於門下。

translations.literal: Together with Ne he went to Hezhong to visit Li Shouzhen; Shouzhen was impressed in conversation with them and housed them both as retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Ne he went to Hezhong to visit Li Shouzhen; Shouzhen was impressed by their conversation and took them both in as retainers.

sentences.zh: 守貞謀叛，遣元與訥間道乞師江南。

translations.literal: When Shouzhen plotted rebellion, he sent Yuan and Ne by secret routes to beg troops from Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouzhen plotted rebellion, he sent Yuan and Ne by secret routes to beg troops from Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 江南遣大將軍皇甫暉等率眾數萬次沐陽，為之聲援。

translations.literal: Jiangnan sent Grand General Huangfu Hui and others leading tens of thousands of troops to encamp at Muyang as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan sent Grand General Huangfu Hui and others with tens of thousands of troops to encamp at Muyang in support.

sentences.zh: 會守貞敗，元與訥留江南。

translations.literal: When Shouzhen was defeated, Yuan and Ne remained in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouzhen was defeated, Yuan and Ne remained in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 元易姓朱，楊訥更姓名為李平。

translations.literal: Yuan changed his surname to Zhu; Yang Ne changed his name and surname to Li Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan changed his surname to Zhu; Yang Ne changed his name and surname to Li Ping.

sentences.zh: 元事李景，歷江寧令、駕部員外郎、文理院待詔，嘗坐事左遷。

translations.literal: Yuan served Li Jing, successively holding the posts of magistrate of Jiangning, Vice Director of the Chariot Office, and text-and-ritual court attendant; he was once demoted for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan served Li Jing as magistrate of Jiangning, Vice Director of the Chariot Office, and text-and-ritual court attendant, and was once demoted for an offense.

sentences.zh: 世宗征淮南，諸郡多下，元求見言兵事，景大悅，遣率兵攻舒州，復之，即以為團練使。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned in Huainan and many commanderies fell, Yuan requested an audience to speak on military affairs; Jing was greatly pleased, sent him to lead troops to attack Shuzhou, recovered it, and immediately made him regimental training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong campaigned in Huainan and many commanderies fell, Yuan requested an audience to discuss military affairs; Jing was greatly pleased, sent him to recover Shuzhou, and immediately made him regimental training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又平歷陽，景以元為淮南北面招討使。

translations.literal: He also pacified Liyang; Jing appointed Yuan Commander for the Northern Shore of the Huai for Receiving Surrenders.
translations.idiomatic: He also pacified Liyang, and Jing appointed him commander for receiving surrenders on the north bank of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 周師圍壽春，景以其弟齊王景達為元帥，率兵來救，以陳覺為監軍，總軍政。

translations.literal: When Zhou forces besieged Shouchun, Jing made his younger brother, Prince of Qi Jingda, supreme commander and sent him with troops to the rescue; Chen Jue was made army supervisor with overall authority over military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou forces besieged Shouchun, Jing made his younger brother, Prince of Qi Jingda, supreme commander and sent him to the rescue, with Chen Jue as army supervisor holding overall military and civil authority.

sentences.zh: 元素與覺有隙，覺密表譖元於景，信之，立遣大將楊守忠代元。

translations.literal: Yuan had bad blood with Jue; Jue secretly memorialized slander against Yuan to Jing, who believed it and immediately sent Grand General Yang Shouzhong to replace Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Jue were at odds; Jue secretly slandered Yuan to Jing, who believed him and immediately sent Grand General Yang Shouzhong to replace Yuan.

sentences.zh: 元憤怒，自以戰功高，又不忍負景，欲自殺。

translations.literal: Yuan was furious; considering his military achievements great yet unable to bear betraying Jing, he wished to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was furious; proud of his military achievements yet unable to bear betraying Jing, he wished to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 門下客宋洎諫曰：「大丈夫何往不取富貴，豈必為妻子死哉！

translations.literal: A retainer, Song Ji, remonstrated: "A great man can win wealth and rank wherever he goes — must he die for wife and children!"
translations.idiomatic: A retainer, Song Ji, remonstrated: "A great man can win wealth and rank wherever he goes—must he die for wife and children!"

sentences.zh: 」元聽之，將其眾歸世宗，景盡誅其妻子。

translations.literal: " Yuan heeded him, took his troops over to Shizong, and Jing executed all his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan heeded him, took his troops over to Shizong, and Jing executed his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 世宗素知元驍果，得之甚喜，以為檢校太保、蔡州防禦使。

translations.literal: Shizong had long known Yuan to be fierce and resolute; greatly pleased to obtain him, he made him Grand Guardian by inspection and defense commissioner of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had long known Yuan to be fierce and resolute; greatly pleased to obtain him, he made him Grand Guardian by inspection and defense commissioner of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，改濠州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, he was changed to defense commissioner of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified, he was made defense commissioner of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，從平李重進，改沂州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he followed in the pacification of Li Chongjin and was changed to defense commissioner of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song he took part in suppressing Li Chongjin and was made defense commissioner of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 為滑州巡檢使，與節帥不協，誣奏元為同產妹婿宋玘請求。

translations.literal: As patrol commissioner of Huazhou, he did not get along with the military commissioner and falsely memorialized that Yuan had solicited favors for Song Qi, husband of his sister born of the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: As patrol commissioner of Huazhou, he clashed with the military commissioner and falsely accused Yuan of soliciting favors for Song Qi, husband of his full sister.

sentences.zh: 事得釋。

translations.literal: The matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was cleared.

sentences.zh: 詔元復姓舒氏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuan to restore the surname Shu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yuan to restore the surname Shu.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，為白波兵馬都監。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao, he became overall supervisor of the Baibo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao he became overall supervisor of the Baibo Army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，卒，年五十五，特贈武泰軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, he died, aged fifty-five; he was specially posthumously granted the military commission of the Wutai Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he died, aged fifty-five; he was posthumously granted the military commission of the Wutai Army.

sentences.zh: 元辯捷強記，治郡日，或奏其不親獄訟，事多冤滯。

translations.literal: Yuan was quick-witted with a strong memory; while administering a prefecture, someone memorialized that he did not personally hear legal cases and that many matters suffered wrongful delay.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was quick-witted and had a strong memory; while governing a prefecture, someone reported that he did not personally hear legal cases and that many cases were wrongly delayed.

sentences.zh: 太祖面詰問之，凡所詰，元必具誦款占，指述曲直，太祖甚嘉歎之。

translations.literal: Taizu personally questioned him; for every question, Yuan would fully recite the particulars of the case and explain right and wrong; Taizu greatly praised and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu questioned him in person; for every question Yuan fully recited the particulars of the case and explained right and wrong, and Taizu greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 子知白、知雄、知崇。

translations.literal: His sons were Zhibai, Zhixiong, and Zhichong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhibai, Zhixiong, and Zhichong.

sentences.zh: 知白至作坊使。

translations.literal: Zhibai rose to the post of Commissioner of the Craft Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibai rose to Commissioner of the Craft Workshops.

sentences.zh: 知雄初補殿直，雷有終薦授供奉官、鄜延路駐泊都監，後辭疾居嵩山。

translations.literal: Zhixiong was initially appointed as Palace Guard; Lei Youzhong recommended him and he was appointed Attendant Officer and overall supervisor of stationed forces on the Fuyan Circuit route; later citing illness he retired to Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiong was initially appointed Palace Guard; Lei Youzhong recommended him for Attendant Officer and overall supervisor of stationed forces on the Fuyan route, and later citing illness he retired to Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 知白嘗奏事太宗，語及之，即召出，授西京作坊副使、泉福都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Zhibai once reported to affairs before Taizong; when the conversation touched on him, Zhixiong was immediately summoned out and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Craft Workshops and overall patrol commissioner of Quan and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhibai once reported to Taizong and the conversation touched on him, Zhixiong was immediately summoned and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Western Capital Craft Workshops and overall patrol commissioner of Quan and Fu.

sentences.zh: 真宗初，懇請入道，歸嵩陽舊隱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenzong's reign, he earnestly requested to enter the Way and returned to his old hermitage at Songyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenzong's reign he earnestly asked to enter the Way and returned to his old hermitage at Songyang.

sentences.zh: 復為王嗣宗、李元則所薦，授供備庫使，歷知棣州、麟府鄜延鈐轄，又知虔州。

translations.literal: He was again recommended by Wang Sizong and Li Yuanze, appointed Commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Storehouse, successively administered Dizhou and served as overall military controller of Lin Prefecture and the Fuyan Circuit, and also administered Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again recommended by Wang Sizong and Li Yuanze, appointed Commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Storehouse, governed Dizhou, served as overall military controller of Lin Prefecture and the Fuyan Circuit, and also governed Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 復求入道，面賜紫冠服，號崇玄大師。

translations.literal: He again asked to enter the Way; he was personally granted purple cap and robes and given the title Great Master Chongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to enter the Way; the emperor personally granted him purple cap and robes and gave him the title Great Master Chongxuan.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻《字母圖》，有詔褒獎。

translations.literal: He once presented the Alphabet Diagram; an edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented the Alphabet Diagram and received an edict praising and rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年，卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianxing, he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianxing he died, aged eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 知崇累歷內職，至供備庫使。

translations.literal: Zhichong held successive inner-court posts, rising to Commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichong held successive inner-court posts, rising to Commissioner of the Supply and Equipment Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 嘗為廣州鈐轄、河北安撫副使，卒。

translations.literal: He once served as overall military controller of Guangzhou and vice commissioner for pacification of Hebei; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as overall military controller of Guangzhou and vice commissioner for pacification of Hebei, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 知白子昭遠，大中祥符五年，任大理評事，因對自陳，改大理寺丞，賜進士第，至太常博士。

translations.literal: Zhibai's son Zhaoyuan, in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, served as judicial reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review; in an audience he stated his case himself, was changed to Court Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, granted jinshi standing, and rose to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibai's son Zhaoyuan, in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, served as judicial reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review; in an audience he stated his case himself, was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, granted jinshi standing, and rose to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 韓熙載字叔言，濰州北海人。

translations.literal: Han Xizai, courtesy name Shuyan, was a native of Beihai in Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xizai, courtesy name Shuyan, was a native of Beihai in Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光中，舉進士，名聞京、洛。

translations.literal: During the Tongguang era of Later Tang, he passed the jinshi examination and his fame spread through the capital and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang era of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination and his fame spread through the capital and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 父光嗣，為平盧軍節度副使。

translations.literal: His father Guangsi was military commissioner deputy of the Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangsi was deputy military commissioner of the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 同光末，青州軍亂，逐其帥符習，推光嗣為留後。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongguang, the Qingzhou army mutinied, drove out its commander Fu Xi, and set up Guangsi as acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tongguang the Qingzhou army mutinied, drove out its commander Fu Xi, and set up Guangsi as acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，誅光嗣，熙載奔江南，歷偽吳滁、和、常三州從事。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he executed Guangsi; Xizai fled to Jiangnan and successively served as aide in the three prefectures of Chu, He, and Chang under false Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne he executed Guangsi; Xizai fled to Jiangnan and successively served as aide in Chu, He, and Chang prefectures under Wu.

sentences.zh: 李昪僭號，為秘書郎，令事其子景於東宮。

translations.literal: When Li Bian usurped the imperial title, Xizai became Secretary of the Palace Library and was ordered to serve Bian's son Jing in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bian usurped the imperial title, Xizai became Secretary of the Palace Library and was assigned to serve Bian's son Jing in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 景嗣位，遷虞部員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: When Jing succeeded to the throne, Xizai was promoted to Vice Director of the Works Office and historiographer of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing succeeded to the throne, Xizai was promoted to Vice Director of the Works Office and historiographer of the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 熙載自言：「受知遇，不得顯位，是以我屬嗣君也。

translations.literal: Xizai said of himself: "Having received kindness and favor yet not been given a prominent post, that is why you entrusted me to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai said of himself: "I received your kindness and favor yet was not given a prominent post; that is why you entrusted me to the heir.

sentences.zh: 」遂上章，言事切直，景嘉納之。

translations.literal: " He then submitted a memorial; his words were forthright and cutting, and Jing welcomed and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted a memorial with forthright advice, which Jing welcomed.

sentences.zh: 又改吉凶儀禮不如式者十數事，大為宋齊丘、馮延己所忌。

translations.literal: He also corrected more than ten matters in which auspicious and inauspicious rites were not in proper form, greatly incurring the resentment of Song Qiqiu and Feng Yanji.
translations.idiomatic: He also corrected more than ten irregularities in auspicious and inauspicious rites, greatly incurring the resentment of Song Qiqiu and Feng Yanji.

sentences.zh: 昪將葬，以熙載知禮，令兼太常博士。

translations.literal: When Bian was about to be buried, because Xizai understood ritual, he was ordered concurrently to serve as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian was about to be buried, Xizai's knowledge of ritual led to his concurrent appointment as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時江左草創，典禮多闕，議者以繼唐昭宗之後，廟號合稱宗。

translations.literal: At the time the southeast was newly established and many court rituals were lacking; debaters held that since they succeeded after Tang Zhaozong, the temple name ought to be called Zong.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the southeast was newly established and many court rituals were lacking; debaters held that since they succeeded after Tang Zhaozong, the temple name ought to be Zong.

sentences.zh: 熙載建議，以為古者帝王己失之，己得之，謂之反正；

translations.literal: Xizai proposed that in antiquity, when an emperor had himself lost the throne and himself regained it, this was called returning to the correct path;
translations.idiomatic: Xizai proposed that in antiquity, when an emperor had lost the throne himself and regained it himself, this was called returning to the correct path;

sentences.zh: 非我失之，自我復之，謂之中興，中興之君廟號稱祖。

translations.literal: when what one had not oneself lost was restored by oneself, this was called revival; an emperor of revival takes the temple name Zu.
translations.idiomatic: when what one had not lost oneself was restored by oneself, this was called revival, and a reviving emperor takes the temple name Zu.

sentences.zh: 以為興既墜之業，請號烈祖。

translations.literal: Holding that Bian had revived a fallen enterprise, he requested the temple name Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: Holding that Bian had revived a fallen enterprise, he requested the temple name Liezu.

sentences.zh: 景由是益加恩禮，擢知制誥。

translations.literal: Jing therefore increased his favor and ceremony and promoted him to Drafting Edict Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jing therefore increased his honors and promoted him to Drafting Edict Officer.

sentences.zh: 熙載性懶慢，朝直多闕，未幾罷去。

translations.literal: Xizai was by nature lazy and insolent, often absent from court attendance, and before long was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai was lazy and insolent by nature, often absent from court attendance, and was soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，中原多事，江南方盛，其臣陳覺、馮延魯建討福州，師敗而還，景釋不問罪。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun under Jin, the central plains were troubled while the southeast flourished; his ministers Chen Jue and Feng Yanlu proposed attacking Fuzhou; the army was defeated and returned, yet Jing released them without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaiyun under Jin the central plains were in turmoil while the southeast flourished; his ministers Chen Jue and Feng Yanlu proposed attacking Fuzhou; the army was defeated and returned, yet Jing released them without punishment.

sentences.zh: 熙載與徐鉉同上疏，請置於法。

translations.literal: Xizai and Xu Xuan jointly submitted a memorial requesting that they be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai and Xu Xuan jointly submitted a memorial asking that they be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 覺、延魯，宋齊丘之黨也。

translations.literal: Jue and Yanlu were partisans of Song Qiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jue and Yanlu were partisans of Song Qiqiu.

sentences.zh: 熙載為齊丘所排，貶和州司馬，語在《徐鉉傳》。

translations.literal: Xizai was pushed out by Qiqiu and demoted to aide of He Prefecture; the account is in the biography of Xu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai was pushed out by Qiqiu and demoted to aide of He Prefecture; the account appears in the biography of Xu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為虞部郎中、史館修撰，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned as Director of the Works Office, historiographer of the Historiography Institute, and appointed Palace Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was summoned back as Director of the Works Office and historiographer of the Historiography Institute, and appointed Palace Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 世宗平淮甸，景患國用不足，熙載請鑄鐵錢。

translations.literal: When Shizong pacified the Huai region, Jing worried that state revenues were insufficient; Xizai requested casting iron coin.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong pacified the Huai region, Jing worried that state revenues were insufficient, and Xizai proposed casting iron coin.

sentences.zh: 及煜襲位，卒行其議，以熙載為兵部尚書，充鑄錢使。

translations.literal: When Yu succeeded to the throne, the proposal was finally carried out; Xizai was made Minister of War and appointed coin-casting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu succeeded to the throne the proposal was finally carried out; Xizai was made Minister of War and appointed coin-casting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 錢貨益輕，不勝其弊，熙載頗亦自悔。

translations.literal: The currency grew ever lighter and the harm could not be borne; Xizai too came to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: The currency grew ever lighter and the harm became unbearable; Xizai came to regret it himself.

sentences.zh: 熙載善為文，江東士人、道釋載金帛以求銘誌碑記者不絕，又累獲賞賜。

translations.literal: Xizai was skilled at writing; scholars, Daoists, and Buddhists east of the Yangzi continually brought gold and silk seeking inscriptions, epitaphs, and stele records, and he also repeatedly received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai was skilled at writing; scholars, Daoists, and Buddhists east of the Yangzi continually brought gold and silk seeking inscriptions, epitaphs, and stele records, and he also received many rewards.

sentences.zh: 由是畜妓妾四十餘人，多善音樂，不加防閑，恣其出入外齋，與賓客生徒雜處。

translations.literal: Thereby he kept more than forty singing girls and concubines, many skilled in music; he did not restrain them and allowed them to come and go freely to the outer study, mingling with guests, students, and disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he kept more than forty singing girls and concubines, many skilled in music; he did not restrain them and allowed them to come and go freely to the outer study, mingling with guests, students, and disciples.

sentences.zh: 煜以其盡忠言事，垂欲相之，終以帷薄不修，責授右庶子，分司洪州。

translations.literal: Yu, because he spoke loyally on affairs, was on the verge of making him chief minister, but in the end because of disorder in his private quarters demoted him to Right Supervisor of the Heir Apparent and sent him to serve at Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, because Xizai spoke loyally on affairs, was on the verge of making him chief minister, but in the end demoted him to Right Supervisor of the Heir Apparent and sent him to serve at Hongzhou for disorder in his private quarters.

sentences.zh: 熙載盡斥諸妓，單車即路，煜留之，改秘書監，俄而復位。

translations.literal: Xizai dismissed all the singing girls and set out alone in a single cart; Yu kept him back, changed his appointment to Director of the Palace Library, and before long restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai dismissed all the singing girls and set out alone in a single cart; Li Yu kept him back, made him Director of the Palace Library, and soon restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 向所斥之妓稍稍而集，頃之如故。

translations.literal: The singing girls he had dismissed gradually gathered again, and before long things were as before.
translations.idiomatic: The singing girls he had dismissed gradually gathered again, and before long things were as before.

sentences.zh: 煜歎曰：「吾亦無如之何！

translations.literal: Yu sighed and said: "There is nothing I can do about it either!
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu sighed and said: "There is nothing I can do about it either!

sentences.zh: 」遷中書侍郎、光政殿學士承旨。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Academician-in-Attendance of the Hall of Radiant Governance.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Academician-in-Attendance of the Hall of Radiant Governance.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao, he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaibao he died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 煜痛惜之，贈左僕射、平章事，諡文靖，葬於梅嶺岡謝安墓側，命徐鍇集其遺文。

translations.literal: Yu grieved deeply for him, posthumously granted him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor, gave him the posthumous title Wenjing, buried him beside Xie An's tomb on Meiling Ridge, and ordered Xu Kai to compile his remaining writings.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu grieved deeply for him, posthumously granted him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor, gave him the posthumous title Wenjing, buried him beside Xie An's tomb on Meiling Ridge, and ordered Xu Kai to compile his remaining writings.

sentences.zh: 熙載才氣俊逸，機用周敏，性高簡，無所卑屈，未嘗拜人。

translations.literal: Xizai's talent and spirit were outstanding and free; his wit and resourcefulness were thorough and quick; his nature was lofty and austere, bowing to no one, and he never once bowed to another person.
translations.idiomatic: Xizai's talent and spirit were outstanding; his wit was thorough and quick; his nature was lofty and austere, bowing to no one, and he never once bowed to another person.

sentences.zh: 雖被遣逐，終不改節，江左號為「 韓夫子」。

translations.literal: Though sent away in disgrace, he never changed his integrity; the southeast called him "Master Han."
translations.idiomatic: Though sent away in disgrace, he never changed his integrity; the southeast called him "Master Han."

sentences.zh: 顯德中，熙載來朝廷，歸，景問中國大臣，時太祖方典禁兵，熙載對曰：「趙點檢顧視不常，不可測也。

translations.literal: During Xiande, Xizai came to the Song court; on returning, Jing asked about the great ministers of China; at the time Taizu was just in charge of the palace armies; Xizai replied: "Director Zhao's glances are unsettled and cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiande Xizai came to the Song court; on returning, Jing asked about the great ministers of China; at the time Taizu was in charge of the palace armies; Xizai replied: "Director Zhao's glances are unsettled and cannot be fathomed.

sentences.zh: 」及太祖登極，景益重之。

translations.literal: " When Taizu ascended the throne, Jing valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " When Taizu ascended the throne, Jing valued him all the more.

sentences.zh: 頗以文章自負，好大言。

translations.literal: He was rather proud of his literary compositions and fond of grand pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: He was rather proud of his literary compositions and fond of grand pronouncements.

sentences.zh: 初，乾德丁卯年，五星連珠於奎，奎主文章，又在魯分，時太宗鎮兗、海，中國太平之符也。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the dingmao year of Qiande, the five planets aligned in Kui; Kui governs literary composition and also lay in the Lu asterism; at the time Taizong was stationed at Yan and Hai — a sign of peace in China.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the dingmao year of Qiande, the five planets aligned in Kui; Kui governs literary composition and also lay in the Lu asterism; at the time Taizong was stationed at Yan and Hai—a sign of peace in China.

sentences.zh: 是歲，熙載著《格言》五卷，自序其事云：「魯無其應，韓子《格言》成之。

translations.literal: That year Xizai wrote five fascicles of Admonitions; in his own preface to the matter he said: "Lu had no corresponding fulfillment; Master Han's Admonitions completed it.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xizai wrote five fascicles of Admonitions; in his own preface he said: "Lu had no corresponding fulfillment; Master Han's Admonitions completed it.

sentences.zh: 」人多笑之。

translations.literal: " Many people laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: " Many people laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 馮謐本名延魯，字叔文，其先彭城人，唐末南渡，家於新安。

translations.literal: Feng Mi's original name was Yanlu, courtesy name Shuwen; his ancestors were men of Pengcheng; at the end of Tang they crossed south, and the family settled in Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Mi, born Yanlu and styled Shuwen, came from a Pengcheng family that crossed south at the end of Tang and settled in Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 李僭號，立子景為太子，謐與兄延己俱以文學得幸。

translations.literal: When Li usurped a princely title, he established his son Jing as crown prince; Mi and his elder brother Yanji both won favor through literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Li assumed a royal title and made his son Jing crown prince, Mi and his elder brother Yanji both won favor at court through their literary accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 及景嗣位，累遷至中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Jing succeeded to the throne, [Mi] was repeatedly promoted to Drafting Drafter in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing succeeded to the throne, Mi rose through repeated promotions to Drafting Drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，閩越大亂，景遣謐與諫議大夫陳覺乘傳安撫，謐遂矯詔發數郡兵攻福州。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun of Jin, Min and Yue fell into great disorder; Jing sent Mi and Remonstrance and Correction Grandee Chen Jue by relay post to pacify and reassure; Mi then forged an edict and mobilized troops from several prefectures to attack Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jin era Kaiyun, when Min and Yue were torn by rebellion, Jing sent Mi and Remonstrance and Correction Grandee Chen Jue on an urgent pacification mission; Mi then forged an edict and raised troops from several prefectures to attack Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及敗，引佩刀自刺，親吏製之，不死，長流舒州。

translations.literal: When [the expedition] was defeated, he drew his belt knife and stabbed himself; a personal clerk restrained him, and he did not die; he was banished for life to Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign failed, he drew his belt dagger and tried to kill himself; a personal clerk restrained him, and he survived, but was sentenced to lifelong exile in Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會赦敘用，復為中書舍人，改工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Upon an amnesty restoring offenders to office, he again became Drafting Drafter in the Secretariat and was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty restored him to office; he again served as Drafting Drafter in the Secretariat and was then made Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 江南以揚州為東都，命謐副留守。

translations.literal: Jiangnan took Yangzhou as its eastern capital and appointed Mi deputy regional commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan made Yangzhou its eastern capital, Mi was appointed deputy regional commissioner there.

sentences.zh: 周世宗下揚州，謐髡發為僧，匿於佛寺，為官軍所獲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong of Zhou took Yangzhou, Mi shaved his head and became a monk, hiding in a Buddhist temple, and was captured by the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong of Zhou captured Yangzhou, Mi shaved his head, took refuge as a monk in a temple, and was seized by the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 世宗釋之，授太常卿，賜與甚厚。

translations.literal: Shizong released him, appointed him Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and bestowed gifts upon him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong released him, made him Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and rewarded him with extraordinary generosity.

sentences.zh: 數年，拜刑部侍郎，放還，為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Several years later, he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice, sent back [to Jiangnan], and became Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice, sent back to Jiangnan, and then made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，煜遣來貢，因表求舒州田宅，詔賜之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, Yu sent him with tribute; he also submitted a memorial requesting fields and dwellings in Shuzhou, and an edict granted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong, Yu sent him with tribute; Mi also memorialized asking for fields and a residence in Shuzhou, and the court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 後改常州觀察使而卒。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Changzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Military Commissioner of Changzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子伉歸中朝，與兄儀、價並登進士第。

translations.literal: His son Kang returned to the central court; together with his elder brothers Yi and Jia he all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang entered the service of the central court and, together with his elder brothers Yi and Jia, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 伉文辭清麗，嘗著《平晉頌》，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Kang's literary style was clear and refined; he once composed "An Ode on Pacifying Jin," and men of the time praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Kang wrote in a clear, elegant style; his "Ode on Pacifying Jin" won praise from contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中侍御史，歷典藩郡，皆有治跡。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Censor and served successively as prefect of several regions, leaving good records of governance in each.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted repeatedly to Palace Censor, he served in succession as prefect of several regions and left a record of good administration in each.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，知福州，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 特賜錢十萬，錄其子玄應同學究出身。

translations.literal: [The court] specially granted one hundred thousand coins and enrolled his son Xuanying through the classical-studies jinshi route.
translations.idiomatic: The court specially granted one hundred thousand coins and enrolled his son Xuanying through the classical-studies examination route.

sentences.zh: 潘佑，南唐散騎常侍處常之子。

translations.literal: Pan You was the son of Pan Chuchang, Regular Attendant of the Secretariat of Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Pan You was the son of Pan Chuchang, Regular Attendant of the Secretariat under Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 少介僻，杜門讀書，不交人事。

translations.literal: In youth he was aloof and eccentric; he shut his door and read books, mingling in no worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was aloof and eccentric, shut himself in to read, and kept aloof from worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 及長，善屬文，尤長於論議。

translations.literal: When grown, he was skilled at composing prose, and was especially adept at disputation.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he proved skilled at prose composition and was especially forceful in debate.

sentences.zh: 陳喬、韓熙載、徐鉉等共薦於景，為秘書省正字、直崇文館。

translations.literal: Chen Qiao, Han Xizai, Xu Xuan, and others jointly recommended him to Jing; he was made Corrector of the Secretariat and Direct Attendant of the Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qiao, Han Xizai, Xu Xuan, and others jointly recommended him to Jing, and he was appointed Corrector of the Secretariat and Direct Attendant of the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 煜襲位，遷虞部員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: When Yu succeeded to the throne, [You] was transferred to Vice Director of the Revenue Office and Compiler of the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu succeeded to the throne, You was transferred to Vice Director of the Revenue Office and made a compiler at the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知制誥，為內史舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Drafting Drafter and Inner Secretariat Drafting Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Drafting Drafter and then Inner Secretariat Drafting Drafter.

sentences.zh: 有李平者，本嵩山道士楊訥，依河中帥李守貞。

translations.literal: There was a man named Li Ping, originally the Songshan Daoist Yang Ne, who attached himself to the military governor of Hezhong, Li Shouzhen.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Li Ping who had originally been the Songshan Daoist Yang Ne and had attached himself to the Hezhong military governor Li Shouzhen.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，守貞反，遣訥與舒元乞師江南。

translations.literal: In the Qiandyou era of Han, Shouzhen rebelled and sent Ne and Shu Yuan to beg troops from Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Han era Qiandyou, Shouzhen rebelled and sent Ne and Shu Yuan to Jiangnan to beg for troops.

sentences.zh: 守貞敗，訥遂易姓名，江南以為員外郎，遷衛尉少卿、蘄州刺史、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shouzhen was defeated, Ne changed his name; Jiangnan made him a Vice Director and promoted him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia, Prefect of Qizhou, and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouzhen's defeat Ne changed his name; Jiangnan appointed him a Vice Director and later promoted him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia, Prefect of Qizhou, and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 平好神仙修養之事，動作妖妄，自言常與神接。

translations.literal: Ping was fond of immortality and cultivation practices; his actions were uncanny and extravagant, and he claimed he was constantly in contact with spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was obsessed with immortality and self-cultivation; his behavior was uncanny and extravagant, and he claimed to commune constantly with spirits.

sentences.zh: 佑亦好神仙，遂相善。

translations.literal: You also loved immortality, and the two became close.
translations.idiomatic: You shared the same obsession, and the two became close friends.

sentences.zh: 二家皆置淨室，圖神像，常被髮裸袒處室中，家人亦不得至。

translations.literal: Both households set up purified chambers and painted spirit images; they often let their hair hang loose and remained bare-chested in the chambers, and even family members were not allowed to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Both households kept purified chambers painted with spirit images; they often let their hair hang loose and sat bare-chested inside, and even their families were forbidden to enter.

sentences.zh: 又嘗建議復井田，及依《周禮》置牛籍，薦平判司農寺以督之。

translations.literal: He also once recommended restoring the well-field system and establishing a cattle registry according to the Rites of Zhou, and recommended Ping to oversee the Directorate of Agriculture to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: He also once urged restoration of the well-field system and creation of a cattle registry modeled on the Rites of Zhou, recommending Ping to serve concurrently at the Directorate of Agriculture to supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 事行，百姓大撓，未幾而罷。

translations.literal: When the policy was implemented, the common people were greatly agitated; before long it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Once the policy took effect the people were thrown into turmoil, and before long it was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 佑自以為眾所排，因憤怒，歷詆大臣與握兵者兩為朋比，將謀反叛；

translations.literal: You believed himself squeezed out by the multitude; in anger he denounced in turn the great ministers and those who held military power as two factions in league, plotting rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Believing himself ostracized, You grew furious and in turn denounced the chief ministers and the men who held military power as two factions in league, plotting rebellion;

sentences.zh: 又言國將亡，非己為相不可救。

translations.literal: He also said the state was about to perish and that unless he himself became chief minister it could not be saved.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared that the state was doomed and could be saved only if he himself were made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 江南政事多在尚書省，因薦平知省事，又薦星官楊熙澄為樞密使，小校侯英典禁兵，煜不納。

translations.literal: Most of Jiangnan's governance lay in the Department of State Affairs; he therefore recommended Ping to manage its affairs, and also recommended the astronomer Yang Xiguang as Privy Councilor and the petty officer Hou Ying to command the palace guard; Yu did not accept [these recommendations].
translations.idiomatic: Because most of Jiangnan's affairs were handled through the Department of State Affairs, he recommended Ping to manage its business, Yang Xiguang the court astronomer as Privy Councilor, and the petty officer Hou Ying to command the palace guard; Yu rejected all of it.

sentences.zh: 佑益忿，抗疏請誅宰相湯悅等數十人，煜手書教戒之。

translations.literal: You grew all the more resentful and submitted a blunt memorial requesting the execution of Chief Minister Tang Yue and several dozen others; Yu wrote him a letter of admonition in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: You grew still angrier and submitted a blunt memorial demanding the execution of Chief Minister Tang Yue and several dozen others; Yu answered with a handwritten letter of admonition.

sentences.zh: 佑不復朝謁，乃於家上書曰：「臣聞『三軍可奪帥也，匹夫不可奪誌也』。

translations.literal: You no longer attended court audiences; he submitted a memorial from home, saying: "Your subject has heard, 'An army's commander may be taken away, but a common man's resolve may not be taken away.'
translations.idiomatic: You stopped attending court and submitted a memorial from home, saying, "Your subject has heard that 'an army's commander may be removed, but a common man's resolve cannot be broken.'

sentences.zh: 近者連上表章指陳奸惡，何面目以見士人乎？

translations.literal: Of late I have repeatedly submitted memorials exposing treachery and wickedness — with what face can I again appear before men of learning?"
translations.idiomatic: Of late I have repeatedly submitted memorials exposing treachery and wickedness — with what face can I again appear before men of learning?"

sentences.zh: 」遂自縊死。

translations.literal: " With that he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 皇甫繼勳，江州節度使暉之子。

translations.literal: Huangfu Jixun was the son of Military Commissioner of Jiangzhou Huangfu Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Jixun was the son of Huangfu Hui, Military Commissioner of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼以父蔭為軍校，父死難於滁州，累遷將軍、池饒二州刺史，勤於吏事。

translations.literal: In youth, through his father's privilege he became a junior army officer; when his father died in battle at Chuzhou, [Jixun] was repeatedly promoted to general and to prefect of Chi and Rao, and was diligent in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he entered service as a junior army officer through his father's privilege; after his father died in battle at Chuzhou, he rose through repeated promotions to general and to prefect of Chi and Rao, proving diligent in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 入為諸軍都虞候，遷神衛統軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Chief Commandant of All Armies and was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of the Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Chief Commandant of All Armies and was then made Commander-in-Chief of the Divine Guard.

sentences.zh: 諸老將相次皆死，而繼勳尚少，遂為大將。

translations.literal: The old generals and chief ministers died one after another, while Jixun was still young; he thus became a senior commander.
translations.idiomatic: As the old generals and chief ministers died off one after another while Jixun was still relatively young, he came to stand among the realm's senior commanders.

sentences.zh: 貲產優贍，營第舍、車服，畜妓樂，潔飲食，極遊宴之好。

translations.literal: His wealth and property were ample; he built mansions and carriages and robes, kept singing girls and musicians, kept his food cleanly prepared, and indulged to the utmost in feasting and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy and well provided for, he built fine mansions and outfitted himself with carriages and robes, kept singing girls and musicians, insisted on immaculate food, and indulged to the full in feasting and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 及宋師至，諸軍多敗衄，繼勳欲煜之速降，每眾中流言，頗道國中蹙弱。

translations.literal: When the Song army arrived, many armies suffered defeat; Jixun wished Yu would surrender quickly, and in gatherings he spread rumors, largely speaking of the state's weakness and distress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song army arrived and one army after another suffered defeat, Jixun wanted Li Yu to surrender quickly; in public gatherings he spread rumors emphasizing the state's weakness and distress.

sentences.zh: 侄紹傑亦以繼勳故，為巡檢。

translations.literal: His nephew Shao Jie also, on account of Jixun, became a patrol inspector.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Shao Jie also became a patrol inspector through Jixun's influence.

sentences.zh: 常令紹傑入見煜，陳歸命之計。

translations.literal: He often had Shao Jie enter to see Yu and lay out plans for surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He often sent Shao Jie in to see Yu and lay out plans for surrender.

sentences.zh: 會有風雹，繼勳又密陳滅亡之兆。

translations.literal: When there was a storm of wind and hail, Jixun again secretly presented it as an omen of extinction.
translations.idiomatic: When a storm of wind and hail struck, Jixun again secretly presented it to Yu as an omen of extinction.

sentences.zh: 偏裨或有募勇士欲夜出營邀宋師者，輒鞭而拘之。

translations.literal: Among staff officers, some who recruited brave men intending to sally from camp by night to intercept the Song army — he would whip them and detain them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever staff officers recruited brave men intending to sally from camp by night and strike the Song army, he had them whipped and detained.

sentences.zh: 又因請出煜親兵千餘守闕城，為宋師所掩。

translations.literal: He also, on pretext of a request, sent out more than a thousand of Yu's personal guard to defend the gate city, and they were ambushed by the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: He also, under the pretext of a request, sent out more than a thousand of Yu's personal guard to hold the gate city, and they were ambushed by the Song army.

sentences.zh: 一日，煜躬自巡城，見宋師列柵城外，旌旗遍野，始驚懼，知為左右所蔽。

translations.literal: One day Yu personally inspected the walls and saw the Song army's palisades arrayed outside the city, banners and flags covering the fields; only then was he startled and fearful, knowing he had been concealed [from the truth] by those around him.
translations.idiomatic: One day Li Yu personally inspected the walls and saw the Song army's palisades outside the city and banners covering the fields; only then was he shocked and afraid, realizing that those around him had kept him in the dark.

sentences.zh: 及巡城還，繼勳從至宮。

translations.literal: When the wall inspection ended and he returned, Jixun followed him to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the inspection ended and he returned to the palace, Jixun followed him inside.

sentences.zh: 煜乃責其流言惑眾及不用命之狀，收付大理。

translations.literal: Yu then charged him with spreading rumors to confuse the multitude and with disobeying orders, and had him arrested and handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then charged him with spreading rumors to confuse the people and with disobeying orders, and had him arrested and handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 始出，軍士悉集，臠割其肉，頃刻都盡。

translations.literal: As soon as he was led out, soldiers all gathered and cut his flesh in pieces; in an instant it was entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: The moment he was led out, soldiers gathered and cut his flesh to pieces; in an instant nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 紹傑亦被誅。

translations.literal: Shao Jie was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Jie was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 煜皆赦其妻子。

translations.literal: Yu pardoned their wives and children in both cases.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pardoned the wives and children of both men.

sentences.zh: 周惟簡，饒州鄱陽人。

translations.literal: Zhou Weijian was a native of Poyang in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Weijian was a native of Poyang in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 隱居，好學問，明《易》義。

translations.literal: He lived in retirement, loved learning, and was well versed in the meaning of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement, loved learning, and was well versed in the meaning of the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 煜召為國子博士、集賢侍講。

translations.literal: Yu summoned him as Erudite of the Directorate of Education and Attendant Lecturer of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Yu summoned him to serve as Erudite of the Directorate of Education and Attendant Lecturer of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以虞部郎中致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he retired as Director of the Revenue Office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired with the rank of Director of the Revenue Office.

sentences.zh: 宋師圍金陵，煜求能使交兵者，張洎薦惟簡有遠略，可以談笑和解之。

translations.literal: When the Song army besieged Jinling, Yu sought someone who could negotiate a halt to hostilities; Zhang Bi recommended Weijian as having far-reaching strategy and able to resolve matters through easy conversation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song army besieged Jinling, Li Yu sought someone who could negotiate a halt to hostilities; Zhang Bi recommended Weijian as a man of far-reaching judgment who could settle matters through easy conversation.

sentences.zh: 召為給事中，與徐鉉奉使至京師。

translations.literal: [Yu] summoned him as Supervising Censor and sent him with Xu Xuan as envoys to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yu summoned him as Supervising Censor and sent him with Xu Xuan as envoys to the Song capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖召見詰責，惟簡惶恐，反言曰：「臣本居山野，無仕進之意，李煜強遣來耳。

translations.literal: Taizu summoned him for interrogation and rebuke; Weijian, in terror, spoke contrarily, saying: "Your subject originally dwelt in mountain wilds and had no intent to pursue an official career; Li Yu forced me to come."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu summoned him for interrogation and rebuke; terrified, Weijian answered contrarily, saying, "Your subject originally lived in the mountains and had no wish to pursue office; Li Yu forced me to come."

sentences.zh: 臣素聞終南山多靈藥，事寧後，願得棲隱。

translations.literal: Your subject has long heard that Mount Zhongnan has many miraculous drugs; after affairs are settled, I wish to withdraw and live in seclusion there."
translations.idiomatic: I have long heard that Mount Zhongnan holds many miraculous herbs; once affairs are settled, I wish to withdraw there and live in seclusion."

sentences.zh: 」太祖許之。

translations.literal: " Taizu consented.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 江南平，以惟簡為國子《周易》博士、判監事。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, Weijian was made Erudite of the Book of Changes in the Directorate of Education and Concurrent Director.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan was pacified, Weijian was made Erudite of the Book of Changes in the Directorate of Education and given concurrent directorship of the directorate.

sentences.zh: 開寶九年，上書述前誌，求解官，蓋不得已，非其心也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaibao he submitted a memorial recounting his earlier intentions and requesting release from office — this was because he had had no choice, not because it was his heart's desire.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaibao he submitted a memorial recounting his earlier intentions and asking to be released from office — not because he had wanted service, but because he had had no choice.

sentences.zh: 改虞部郎中，致仕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Revenue Office and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Revenue Office and retired.

sentences.zh: 以其子繕為京兆府鄠縣主簿，俾就養。

translations.literal: His son Shan was made Chief Clerk of Hu County in the metropolitan prefecture so that he might attend to [Weijian's] needs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shan was appointed Chief Clerk of Hu County in the metropolitan prefecture so that he could remain nearby and support him.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，惟簡自終南至闕下，求入見。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, Weijian came from Mount Zhongnan to the capital seeking an audience.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taiping Xingguo era, Weijian came from Mount Zhongnan to the capital seeking an audience.

sentences.zh: 有司以致仕官非有詔召無求對之制，乃還。

translations.literal: The relevant office, citing the rule that retired officials without an edict summoning them might not request an audience, sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office, citing the rule that retired officials might not request an audience without an edict summoning them, sent him back.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復上表自求用，除太常博士，遷水部員外郎，卒。

translations.literal: More than a year later he again submitted a memorial requesting employment; he was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, transferred to Vice Director of the Water Office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he again submitted a memorial requesting appointment; he was made Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Vice Director of the Water Office, and died.

sentences.zh: 繕後舉進士，至都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Shan later passed the jinshi examination and rose to Vice Director of the Department of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Shan later passed the jinshi examination and rose to Vice Director of the Department of Justice.
